**Translation to English:**

To the cantor, archdeacon, and sacristan of Vienne. Considering those matters that pertain to God. Our beloved son William of Savoy, procurator of the church of Valence, has presented to us in person that certain Roman emperors, etc., up to: we have deemed it necessary by apostolic authority to confirm the privileges granted to the same church. Therefore, we command that you do not allow the aforementioned church of Valence, as long as it is willing to abide by the law before a competent judge, to be unjustly troubled by anyone regarding these matters. Given at Anagni, on the third day before the nones of July, in the thirteenth year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX cantori, archidiacono et sacriste Viennensibus mandat ut ecclesiam Valentinam, postquam parata fuerit stare juri coram judice competenti, ab indebita molestia non permittant perturbari; privilegia etiam eidem ecclesiae indulta auctoritate apostolica confirmat. Datum Anagnie, III nonas Julii, anno tertiodecimo.

**Translation to English:**

To Master Bernard, our subdeacon, canon of Patras. The petition presented to us by our venerable brother, the bishop of Methoni, stated that Pope Honorius III, of blessed memory, our predecessor, had providently decreed that tithes in those regions should be fully paid. Both the bishop of Albano, of blessed memory, and our beloved son John, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Praxedes, while serving in those regions as legates, had ordered the excommunication of those who unlawfully withheld tithes, as is more fully contained in their constitutions. Our venerable brother, the archbishop of Patras, should therefore pronounce the sentence of excommunication in his province against such withholders. However, our venerable brother, the bishop of Koroni, having no regard for these matters, dares to withhold tithes from the church of Methoni from some estates he holds in the Diocese of Methoni and, bound by the sentence of excommunication, presumptuously celebrates divine services, to the peril of his soul and the scandal of many. Furthermore, supported by the favor of some Franks, he invades the territory of the said diocese, unjustly usurps tithes, certain abbeys, and other revenues, and refuses to return them, causing serious damages and injuries concerning possessions and other matters. But since the aforesaid bishop of Koroni is so powerful in those parts that the bishop of Methoni, as we have learned, cannot contend with him there, we, not wishing for the latter to suffer a loss of his rights, command you to effectively admonish and induce the aforementioned bishop of Koroni to desist from molesting and injuring the bishop of Methoni and his church, and to offer appropriate satisfaction regarding the aforementioned matters. If he contemptuously refuses to comply with your admonition, set a suitable peremptory term for him, within which he must present himself to our presence, either personally or through a suitable procurator, to do and receive what the order of law requires concerning these matters. Notwithstanding the constitution etc., as above. Given at the Lateran, on the 11th day before the Kalends of April, in the third year of our pontificate.

**Regesto (in Latin):**

Gregorius IX Magistro Bernardo, subdiacono suo, canonico Patracensi, mandat ut episcopum Coronensem, qui decimas Methonensi ecclesiae subtrahit et divina celebrat nimis scandalose, moneat et inducat ad desistendum ab iniuriis et satisfactionem debite faciendam, alioquin terminum ei peremptorium statuendo, quo se coram pontifice repraesentet. Datum Laterani, XI kalendas aprilis, anno pontificatus tertio.

**Translation to English:**

To Ofttonil, Cardinal Deacon of Saint Nicholas in Carcere Tulliano, Legate of the Apostolic See. Between our beloved sons, John of Vercelli, our subdeacon and canon of Lincoln, and the archdeacon of Buckingham, a dispute arose concerning the church of the same place in the diocese of Lincoln. After various letters obtained from the Apostolic See to different judges, the matter was litigated for some time under the examination of our beloved son, Egidius, Cardinal Deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian, whom we appointed as auditor for the procurators of the parties involved, concerning the possessory and petitory issues. Then, due to the absence of the same cardinal, we assigned the case to our beloved son Thomas, Cardinal Priest of the Title of Saint Sabina, to hear it. After carefully reviewing the judicial proceedings and hearing the arguments presented before him, and having them faithfully recited in our presence and that of our brothers, concerning the petitory issue, which, due to certain proofs, etc., as above, until: proofs, as reason suggested, nullifying the process conducted by the abbot of Thame and his co-judges, who wrongfully decreed and induced the said archdeacon into possession of the same church under the pretext of certain letters of ours obtained in common form, the mentioned archdeacon and his procurator were condemned by the aforementioned John and his procurator to restore the said church and to pay one hundred marks sterling for the fruits received both before and after the contestation of the suit from the offerings, lands, tithes, and mills of the aforementioned church, by our mandate and the advice of our brothers, suspending the question concerning expenses as it could not be easily distinguished what was done in the prosecution of possession and what in the prosecution of property until the end of the petitory. Since the sentence's words are insufficient if execution does not follow, we command you to ensure its execution. Those opposing, etc. Given.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Papa Gregorius IX Ofttonil, Sancti Nicolai in Carcere Tulliano diacono cardinali et Apostolicae Sedis legato, mandat ut executionem sententiae in causa inter Johannem de Vercellis, subdiaconum nostrum, et archidiaconum de Bukingham super ecclesia in diocesi Lincolniensi perficiat, quae restitutionem ecclesiae et solutionem centum marcarum pro fructibus decernit, contradictionibus non obstantibus. Dat. Laterani, anno sexto decimo, pontificatus nostri, mense Octobri.

**Translation to English:**

To the noble man Godefridus de Villa Harduinil, Prince of Saint James of Andrevilla, etc. As above, up to: they attempted to expel them violently through your castellan of Clermont and hold it thus occupied. Since we have directed our letters to our beloved son, Master Bernard, our subdeacon and canon of Patras, that, if it is so, he should restrain the said master and brothers, etc., we earnestly request and exhort your nobility more strictly, by apostolic letters, ordering that you do not in any way oppose the said master nor allow any of your subjects to oppose, so that the said master and brothers may be able to receive the benefit of restitution, but rather assist him in executing justice in such a manner that we may justly commend your devotion. Given at Anagni, on the calends of September, in the thirteenth year.

**Latin Regesto:**

Papa Honorius III nobili viro Godefrido de Villa Harduinil mandat ne magistro Bernardo, subdiacono et canonico Patracensi, aliquatenus opponat nec subditos suos permittat opponi, quominus magistro et fratribus per restitutionis beneficium subveniatur, sed in executione justitiae suffragetur. Datum Anagnie, kalendis septembris, anno tertiodecimo.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Tournai and the Provost of the Church of Siclinium, Diocese of Tournai. With the Church of Liège being vacant and the votes of the electors divided, some electing our beloved son William of Savoy, procurator of the Church of Valence, and others electing the Provost of Aachen as their pastor, although an appeal was made to our hearing, the said provost, not heeding the appeal, received the regalia [etc., as above, with a few changes, as noted in the letter numbered 4863, up to:] committed offenses, occupying certain castles and other fortifications of it, receiving homage from laymen and oaths from clerics, conferring benefices and prebends, and pronouncing sentences of suspension and excommunication on some clerics and laymen unwilling to acquiesce to his will. When, therefore, the election of the said provost was annulled for reasons of justice, we have provided the aforementioned William to the same church as bishop and pastor, commanding firmly that you declare those sentences, the collations of prebends and benefices to be utterly null, and that those from whom the provost received homages and oaths are not in any way bound to observe them, and that you cause the castles, fortifications, and other possessions detained from the said church, along with the revenues received from them, to be restored to the aforementioned William. Let opposers, etc.; call upon, if necessary, the aid of the secular arm. Given at Lateran, 4th day before the Nones of June, in the thirteenth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX episcopo Tornacensi et preposito ecclesie Sicliniensis mandat ut, post cassationem electionis prepositi Aquensis, Willelmum de Sabaudia in episcopum Leodiensis ecclesiae instituant, sententias et collationes per prepositum factas nullas declarent, et bona ecclesiae restitui faciant. Dat. Laterani, II nonas junii, anno tertiodecimo.

**Translation to English:**

To the sacristan, archdeacon, and precentor of Neumass. Our beloved sons, the abbot and convent of the monastery of Les Vaux-de-Cernay, of the Cistercian order, have shown us through their petition that previously our venerable brother, the bishop of Maguelonne, claimed that the late Raymond, Count of Toulouse, who at that time held the county of Melgueil and Montferrand, presumed to alienate the estate of Pinu and certain other properties belonging to the same county without the consent of the Holy See. Moreover, the said abbot and convent hold these to the prejudice of the Church of Rome and the bishop himself. He obtained our letters instructing you to inquire simply and without the noise of judgment into the truth of these matters, and if you find it to be so, to compel them to restore the aforesaid properties through ecclesiastical censure, disregarding any appeals, notwithstanding letters of confirmation or others obtained from the Holy See that do not fully mention these matters. And although the said abbot and convent have appeared before you upon your citation, nonetheless, while your judgment was pending, the bishop prohibited them from using the mills existing on the same estate, having it proclaimed through his bailiff in the streets and in neighboring churches that no one should go there to grind; otherwise, being greatly burdensome and injurious to them regarding the aforementioned matters. Therefore, the said abbot, compelled to approach our presence, humbly supplicated on behalf of himself and the convent that, since they had peacefully possessed the said estate and certain properties acquired through a just title of purchase and donation, with the consent of the said count, for thirty years and more, and since for these possessions and the estate, on which they constructed a grange with great expenses and labor, the bishop, after the county came to him in the name of the Church of Rome, received an annual rent from them, we should deign to provide paternal support. Therefore, wishing to preserve the rights of the same county, so that the justice of others, and especially those dedicated to divine praise, is not harmed, we command that if it is so, revoking such prohibitions, and restraining the said bishop and his bailiffs by our authority from their injuries, you diligently inquire simply and without the noise of judgment into what is said to be alienated, and the circumstances pertaining to such alienation, and write back to us faithfully what you find, setting a peremptory and suitable term for the said abbot and convent before us, so that we may dispose of what seems expedient regarding this matter. If not all, etc. Given at the Lateran, the second nones of April, in the thirteenth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Papa Honorius III sacristae, archidiacono, et praecentori Neumasensibus mandat ut, revocatis inhibitionibus episcopi Magalonensis, de alienatione mansi de Pinu et possessionum comitatus Melgorii et Montis Ferrandi a Raymundo comite Tolosano facta, veritatem inquirant et nobis rescribant, assignato termino peremptorio abbati et conventui Vallium Francarum comparendi coram nobis. Datum Laterani, II nonas Aprilis, anno tertiodecimo.

Translation to English:

To the provincial prior of the Order of Preachers of the diocese of Lund. Since, as our venerable brother, the Archbishop of Lund, has taken care to inform us, the laypeople of the diocese of Lund, with the consent of the prelates, have determined that certain payment should be made to the ministers of the bishops for their work in the dedication of churches, which cannot be demanded from the laypeople nor received without the fault of simony, and many clergy of the diocese of Lund have fallen into this fault: by the authority of these presents, we grant you the power to dispense with them in this matter, after first imposing salutary penance and upon its completion, if their life and conduct are deemed honorable, for this time. Given at Anagni, on the ninth day before the calends of September, in the thirteenth year [of our pontificate].

Latin Regesto:

Papa Gregorius IX priori provinciali ordinis fratrum Predicatorum Lundensis diocesis mandat ut, cum laici Lundensis diocesis, accedentibus voluntatibus prelatorum, certum salarium ministris episcoporum in dedicationibus ecclesiarum pro labore suo statuerint, quod absque vitio symoniae exigi vel recipi non potest, et quamplures clerici Lundensis diocesis in hujusmodi reatum inciderint, auctoritate sibi concessa, cum eis, imposita primitus penitentia salutari eaque peracta, si vita et conversatio honesta exegerit, dispensare possit. Dat. Anagnie, VIIII kalendas septembris, anno tertiodecimo.

**Translation to English:**

To the bishop, dean of Valeria, and cantor of Sion. Gerard, rector of the church of Muret, presented a petition to us stating that when our venerable brother, the bishop of Lausanne, his diocesan, accused him of a defect of birth and forced him to resign from the church, it was argued on his behalf that since the same bishop had dispensed with this defect, being born of unmarried parents, by apostolic authority, and had subsequently promoted him to subdeacon and deacon, and conferred the said church upon him, he could not be compelled to resign due to the aforementioned defect. Since the bishop unjustly refused to hear him on this matter, the rector felt wronged and appealed to us. Yet, the bishop disregarded his legitimate appeal, removed him from the administration of the church, and issued a sentence of excommunication against him. Therefore, he petitioned us to restore him to the church and to lift the sentence of excommunication. When the letters obtained in this matter were read, the bishop, through his proctor, opposed them in a public audience, and in the presence of our venerable brother, the bishop of Tusculum, auditor of the matter, stated in opposition that while he had dispensed with Gerard over his defect of birth, promoting him to subdeacon and deacon, and had committed the aforesaid church to him for temporal matters since he did not seem suitable for the care of souls, he had given him hope that if he made himself worthy, he would ordain him as a priest, instructing him to devote himself to studies for a time. However, since Gerard did not pursue scholarly disciplines but instead frequented taverns and played dice, living a dishonest life, the bishop interdicted him from receiving the goods of the church, threatening excommunication if he presumed otherwise. Gerard, contemptuous of this sentence, did not cease to receive the revenues of the church, thus incurring the excommunication. Additionally, the bishop urgently requested that since the Apostolic See decreed that no son or grandson of Gerard's father should be admitted to ecclesiastical benefice or office because he violently attacked the bishop and several priests and gravely injured the church of Lausanne, this decree and the aforementioned sentence of excommunication should be firmly observed against Gerard. Since we are not convinced of the premises, we command that, having summoned the parties, etc. If not all, etc. Given at the Lateran, 6th Ides of April, in the thirteenth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX episcopo, decano de Valeria et cantori Sedunensibus mandat ut, partibus convocatis, causam inter Gerardum, rectorem ecclesiae de Muret, et Lausanensem episcopum audiant et cognoscant super defectu natalium et excommunicationis sententia. Cum episcopus Lausanensis Gerardum natalium defectu accusaret et ab administratione ecclesiae amoveret, Gerardus ad Sedem Apostolicam appellavit. Episcopus tamen sententiam excommunicationis in Gerardum promulgavit ob inhonestam vitam eius. Dat. Laterani, VI idus aprilis, anno tertiodecimo.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Auria. When the pallium, the insignia of the pontifical office, was requested from us with due insistence on behalf of our beloved son John, the elected Archbishop of Compostela, through his envoys, the esteemed sons A. Velasci, the archdeacon, and J. Petri, a canon of Compostela: we, granting his supplications, have decided to send it, taken from the body of blessed Peter, to you through these same envoys. Therefore, we command you to assign it to him according to the form noted below, and receive from him, in the form we have also inserted in the present letters, the oath of fidelity in our name and that of the Roman Church. You should ensure that the form of the oath he will take is sent to us as soon as possible through his open letters, signed with his seal, and by his own messenger. The form for giving the pallium is this: For the honor of Almighty God, the blessed Virgin Mary, the blessed Apostles Peter and Paul, our lord Pope Gregory, the Roman Church, and also the church entrusted to you, we bestow upon you the pallium, taken from the body of blessed Peter, as the fullness of the pontifical office, to be used within your church on specific days which are expressed in the privileges granted by the Apostolic See. The form of the oath is as follows: I, John, Archbishop of Compostela, from this hour forward, etc., to the end. Given at the Lateran, on the ninth day before the calends of July, in the thirteenth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX episcopo Auriensi mandat ut pallium, insignia pontificalis officii, Johanni, Compostellano electo, tradat, et ab ipso juramentum fidelitatis recipiat. Datum Laterani, VIIII kalendas julii, anno tertiodecimo.

**Translation to English:**

To the priors of Rochester and Saint Augustine's in Canterbury, and the archdeacon of Rochester. Our beloved sons, the abbot and convent of Westminster in London, of the Order of Saint Benedict, have brought to our attention through a petition that pertains directly to the Roman Church without any intermediary. They have been granted a privilege by the Apostolic See to freely assign the church of Aiswell, located in the diocese of Lincoln, in which they hold the right of patronage, for the support of brothers, incoming guests, and the poor, whenever it becomes vacant, by appointing a suitable vicar. This vicar is to be sustained by a suitable portion from the goods and resources of the church itself, so that he may sustain himself honorably and bear all burdens of the diocesan, archdeacon, and their officials, as well as other obligations. Henceforth, no one is allowed to remove the church from such a use through any audacity, as they are also fortified by another privilege of the Apostolic See. This privilege ensures that in no church where they are known to hold the right of patronage can anyone be provided for through apostolic letters unless these letters are directed to them and make express mention of this privilege. Recently, as the rector of the church of Aiswell departed this life, the abbot and convent assigned the church to the aforementioned use and requested to be inducted into possession of the church by our venerable brother, the bishop of Lincoln, the diocesan authority. They presented a suitable person for the vicarage to him. They appealed to our audience to prevent him from conferring the church to anyone else to their prejudice or attempting anything against the aforementioned privileges presented before him. However, the bishop, disregarding these privileges and the appeal, claimed to have received an apostolic mandate concerning the provision for Nicholas, a cleric of his diocese, which did not mention the abbot and convent. He presumed to confer the church on Nicholas, a deed he could not rightfully do. He then promulgated sentences of excommunication against the abbot and certain monks and their servants for entering the possession of the said church to protect their rights, and imposed an interdict on the mentioned church. Therefore, we command that if this is so, you declare the sentences of excommunication and interdict to be utterly null and void, and the collation made by the bishop concerning the aforementioned church to be invalid. Remove any unlawful holder from it and induct the named abbot and convent into possession of the same church, defending them once inducted. Given at the Lateran, on the 16th day before the Kalends of May, in the thirteenth year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX prioribus Roffensi et Sancti Augustini Cantuariensis, et archidiacono Roffensi mandat ut, si constiterit, sententias excommunicationis et interdicti a episcopo Lincolniensi contra abbatem et conventum Westmonasterii promulgatas nullas esse denuntient, et collationem ecclesiae de Aiswelle a dicto episcopo Nicolao clerico factam non valere declarent, atque abbati et conventui in possessionem inducant et inductos defendant. Dat. Laterani, XVI kalendas maii, anno tertiodecimo.

**Translation to English:**

To the dean of Troyes. The noble men Peter and Paul Magalotti, Roman merchants, have made a petition to us, stating that Angelus Magalotti, from whom they inherit, had lent a certain sum of money to Peter de Roy, a monk and procurator of the prior and convent of the monastery of Saint Geremarius of Flavigny of the order of Saint Benedict, who had a special mandate from the prior and convent concerning this matter as well as to contract a loan, in accordance with the constitution of two days established in the general council. However, the prior and convent alleged that the said monk, through certain false letters fabricated in their name, presumed to contract a certain huge debt with reckless audacity, and they were being pressed by creditors for its settlement. They obtained letters from us addressed to the dean of Beauvais and his fellow judges concerning this matter, without specifying the name of any creditor, before whom the said prior and convent asserted that the aforementioned merchants were demanding from them a significant debt contracted by the monk using false letters, and requested that the merchants show reason why the monastery should be obligated to settle the said debt or that silence be imposed upon their claim. On behalf of the merchants, it was argued that since it is unjust for anyone to be forced to plead or accuse, they should neither be compelled by such letters to provide the aforementioned reasons, nor should the prior and convent be constrained to pay the debt, whose due date had not yet arrived, as demanded by the merchants. Therefore, it seemed superfluous to request that silence be imposed on their claim for the aforementioned debt, for which they had not yet taken action against the prior and convent. But since the judges, refusing to hear the merchants on the aforementioned matters, nevertheless dragged them to an unsafe place, denying them a more secure venue contrary to justice, they humbly requested recourse; feeling unduly aggrieved by these actions, they appealed to our authority, to which the judges humbly deferred. Therefore, the aforesaid merchants have humbly petitioned us to provide a remedy, as the term has now elapsed, and they have not been paid the money owed, thereby incurring severe damages and expenses. Therefore, we command that if you find that the letters concerning the debt are genuine, you are to compel the said prior and convent to satisfy the merchants for the aforesaid sum, with just and moderate expenses and due compensation for damages, with interest entirely ceasing, as they are bound to do, notwithstanding the aforesaid constitution, ensuring that neither party is dragged beyond the third or fourth (diocese) outside their own diocese for judgment. But if you determine that the letters are false, impose silence on the merchants regarding the debt and do not permit them to further harass the prior and convent on this matter; punish the harassers, etc. Given at the Lateran, 10th day before the Kalends of April, in the 13th year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Papa Honorius III mandat decano Trecensi ut, si invenerit litteras de debito esse veras, priorem et conventum monasterii Sancti Geremarii compellat ad satisfactionem mercatoribus Petro et Paulo Magalotti pro pecunia cum expensis justis et moderatis, constitutione non obstante; sin autem litteras falsas esse constiterit, silentium imponat mercatoribus et priorem et conventum ulterius non molestari permittat. Dat. Laterani, X kalendas aprilis, anno tertiodecimo.

Translation to English:

To Master W. de Cugenho, rector of the church of Weston in the diocese of Lincoln. We gladly acknowledge him because, as we have received from the credible testimony of trustworthy sources, you, noble by birth, are worthy of the gift of grace by your merits of honesty and knowledge, to the cultivation of which you are said to have devoted yourself so arduously that you have deserved to ascend the master's chair in the arts, likewise commendably advancing in canon and civil law. We, moved by the prayers of your devotion, allow you by the authority of these presents, that with your church of Weston, having the care of souls attached and which, as you assert, scarcely exceeds an annual value of twelve marks of silver, you may receive one other benefice, having similar care, if it is canonically offered to you, and freely retain it along with the former, notwithstanding the constitution of the general council; provided that you personally serve in one of them and cause to be served by a suitable vicar in the other. Given at Montfort, on the 7th day before the ides of July, in the thirteenth year.

Regesto in Latin:

Papa Honorius III magistro W. de Cugenho, rectori ecclesiae de Weston, Lincolniensis dioecesis, indulget ut, cum ecclesia sua de Weston, habente curam animarum, duodecim marcarum argentum vix excedente, unicum aliud beneficium similem curam habens recipere valeat, non obstante constitutione concilii generalis; ita quod in uno personaliter deserviat et in alio per idoneum vicarium faciat deserviri. Datum apud Montemfortinum, VII idus Iulii, anno tertiodecimo.

**Translation to English:**

To the bishop of Amiens. In your presence, it is indeed unnecessary to expound in writing about our dear son, Master Riccfard, canon of Amiens and chaplain of our dear son Robert, cardinal deacon of St. Eustace, as you are already acquainted with his integrity. He has long devoted himself to the cultivation of knowledge, striving to render himself commendable. Therefore, since he is also your brother, it should be agreeable to you to pursue him with a special gift of grace. We earnestly entreat and encourage your brotherhood, through apostolic writings, instructing you to ensure that if, as he claims, he desires to add the treasure of sacred scripture to himself, which he is more likely to obtain the more he seems to have fully advanced in other matters, you provide for him in one of the better prebends of the church of Amiens, if it is currently vacant or as soon as the opportunity arises, for the sake of our and the Apostolic See's reverence. Otherwise, we grant letters to our beloved sons, the archdeacon and provost of Arras, instructing them to execute this apostolic mandate. Opponents, etc. We indeed declare null and void anything attempted concerning this prebend outside our mandate. Given at the Lateran, on the eighth day before the ides of June, in the thirteenth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Papa episcopo Ambianensi mandat ut, pro reverentia Sedis Apostolicae, Magistro Riccfardo, canonico Ambianensi et capellano dilecti filii Roberti, cardinalis diaconi Sancti Eustachii, in uno de melioribus personatibus ecclesiae Ambianensis provideat, si vacat aut cum facultas se obtulerit; alioquin archidiacono et praeposito Atrebatensibus mandat ut idem exsequantur. Si quid contra mandatum apostolicum fuerit attemptatum, irritum decernit. Datum Laterani, sextodecimo idus Iunii, anno tertiodecimo.

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop of Messina. When formerly our venerable brother, the Bishop of Marsico, brought a case against the beloved sons, the abbot and convent of the monastery of Casemari of the Cistercian order, concerning the episcopal rights of the churches of Saint Nicholas de Capellis, Saint Rufinus de Archipetra, Saint Magnus, and Saint Nicholas de Castulfi, of the Marsican diocese, before our beloved son Ottone, deacon cardinal of Saint Nicholas in Carcere Tulliano, whom we appointed as auditor: Finally, a definitive sentence was pronounced by the same cardinal against them regarding the said rights. They sought to be provided with full restitution against the aforesaid sentence. And when we appointed our beloved son, the presbyter cardinal of the title of Saint Lawrence in Lucina, as the auditor for these matters, then, with the advice of our brothers, granting a special grace to the aforesaid monastery, we decided to grant to the said bishop, in the aforementioned church of Saint Nicholas de Capellis, a fourth of the tithes and mortuaries, and ten Provenzal solidi and six in others for annual procuration, reserving nothing further in these churches for the said bishop and the Marsican church, with our venerable brother, the Bishop of Alatri, appointed as executor of this provision: The same bishop, as made known to us by the said abbot and convent, personally approached the aforementioned churches and, executing this provision, pronounced a sentence of excommunication against contradictors and rebels, as justice required. But the clerics of the aforementioned church of Saint Nicholas de Capellis, assuming a spirit of rebellion, against the mandate of the said bishop, hold and refuse to return the keys and other goods of the church, and, being bound by such excommunication, presume to perform divine offices, indeed, profane them as much as they can. Given at the Lateran, the sixth day before the Kalends of June, in the thirteenth year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX archiepiscopo Messanensi mandat ut provisionem interpositae sententiae, qua monasterio Casemarii quartam partem decimarum et mortuariorum in ecclesia Sancti Nicolai de Capellis concessit, exsequatur, clericis huius ecclesiae, qui claves et bona detinent, ac rebelles divina officia celebrantes, excommunicatione innodatis; dat. Laterani, VI kalendas junii, anno tertiodecimo.

**Translation to English:**

To the archdeacons of Segovia and Colares, and the cantor of Segovia. Our venerable brother, the Archbishop of Toledo, humbly petitioned us to recall a case to the Apostolic examination that has long been pending between him and the Master and brothers of the Order of Calatrava, of the Cistercian Order, in the diocese of Toledo. The case concerns obedience, certain churches, tithes of royal revenues in Calatrava and other places or towns within the same diocese, as well as tithes of granaries and mills, liberties of clergy, undue tolls and exactions, and other articles. The case had dragged on for over ten years before various judges with apostolic authority without reaching a proper conclusion or even to the point of contestation. Desiring to bring an end to these disputes, we commissioned our beloved sons, the abbot and prior of Valle delle Chiese of the same order, by our letters to summon the Master and brothers to appear before us, either in person or through a suitable representative, with privileges and other documents they possess, within a year from their citation, to receive from the Archbishop the completion of justice on the aforementioned matters. Since it is our intention that such a provision should have the strength of perpetual firmness, and it is just that it, wisely made and willingly received by the parties, should be observed by the aforesaid Peter and the same count, as he has succeeded in burden and honor, we command through apostolic letters to your discretion that you effectively induce them to its observance concerning all and each of the aforementioned articles, compelling them to it by ecclesiastical censure, if necessary, setting aside any appeal. Furthermore, since our venerable brother, the bishop of Nantes, as he himself put forward before us, is oppressed by the same counts in the aforementioned articles, and for this reason, the said provision, containing canonical equity which we made for the liberty of the Breton churches, should rightfully support him as it does the aforementioned prelates, we wish and command that it be extended to the same bishop. Notwithstanding the constitution concerning two days' notice issued in the general council, or if the same nobles have been granted by us that no one can be summoned through apostolic letters for excommunication or interdict, etc., as noted above in previous letters numbered 4877 up to the point: they cannot be summoned through apostolic letters. If not both, etc. Given at the Lateran, the fifth day before the Kalends of May, in the thirteenth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX decano et magistro scholarum Cenomanensibus mandat ut nobiles viri, Johannes, comes Britannie, et predecessores ejus, provisiones factas de libertate ecclesiastica observare compellantur, non obstantibus appellationibus, et hac provisione ad episcopum Nannetensem extenditur. Dat. Laterani, V kalendas Maii, anno tertiodecimo.

To the Chapter of Beauvais. Your church has long been without the solace of a shepherd, following the election held for the dean of that church. P., the archdeacon, and Master Andreas, canon of Beauvais, came to the Apostolic See. They, along with Masters Tthl., canon of Beauvais, and P. de Sparnaco, who were the procurators of those who had elected the dean, presented their case before us regarding the election of the dean. It was proposed that after the bishop of Beauvais of blessed memory had passed, on the appointed day for election, all those who should, could, and wanted to be present, were present, some personally, and others through lawfully appointed procurators due to just impediments. As customary, after the invocation of the Holy Spirit's grace and various discussions, three trustworthy members of the college were selected to conduct the election, under the condition that no election be held unless canonical, and that no ineligible person be elected. To prevent the scrutineers from altering their votes to the injury of others or increasing the votes of their preferred candidate, it was decreed in the chapter that each of them secretly express their vote in a sealed slip before proceeding to scrutiny. After the scrutiny, it emerged that out of thirty-nine canons, thirty directed their votes to the said dean, while six voted for the dean of Paris, and three voted singularly for different candidates. The treasurer of Beauvais, who was then the highest-ranking member after the dean in the chapter, was granted the power by the said thirty and two of the singular voters to elect the dean as bishop in their stead, despite six dissenters refusing to consent to the election. The dean, after much urging, consented to the election made for him. Masters P. and Tfhl. humbly petitioned us to confirm this election as canonically conducted, through the kindness of the Apostolic See. However, the archdeacon and Master Andreas argued against this, claiming that the election was conducted unlawfully and in violation of the appeals that no election should proceed unless canonical, and no unsuitable person be elected due to various flaws such as perjury or other deficiencies. They pointed out that the dean and the majority of nominators had celebrated publicly and solemnly in the interdicted church, and that the dean, after the election, had lifted the interdict on his authority without making satisfaction, even incurring the mark of irregularity by handing over a captured malefactor for execution, thereby rendering the election void. They sought a declaration from us to nullify the election and allow free election rights for their party. Since we were not certain about these matters, we commissioned the venerable bishop of Senlis and his colleagues to summon the necessary parties, hear the arguments, and send the case back to us sufficiently informed. After examining the case, we confirmed the election. Therefore, we command your community by apostolic writ to devoutly receive him as the shepherd of your souls, and humbly heed his wholesome admonitions and mandates. Otherwise, the sentence he pronounces against the rebels will be ratified by us and observed until due satisfaction is achieved. Given at Anagni, 16th Kalends of September, in the thirteenth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Papa Gregorius IX Capitulo Belvacensi mandat ut noviter electum episcopum, decanum ipsius ecclesiae, diligenter recipiant et eius monitis obediant; electionem confirmatam esse declarat. Datum Anagnie, XVI kalendas septembris, anno tertiodecimo.

To Master Bernard, our subdeacon, canon of Patras. J., master, and J. and R., brothers of the hospital of Saint James of Andrevilla, presented in our presence that, although the hospital was established for the reception of the poor and sick, the preceptor and brothers of the house of Saint Mary of the Germans from the regions of Romania, wishing to appropriate it for their own uses, have occupied it unjustly, supported by the favor of the noble prince of Achaea, who acts as its patron. They coerced some brothers from their obedience and imprisoned the said master in custody, not without laying violent hands on him. They also procured a petition on behalf of the said prince in our presence, claiming that the hospital was so spiritually and temporally collapsed that it was believed it could only be easily reformed by their order and that the master and brothers of the hospital wished to transfer to that order, omitting the fact that they had already occupied it, as expressed above, and that they detained the same master in prison. They obtained a mandate from our letters for our venerable brother, the Bishop of Coron, and his colleagues, that if the matter were as stated, they should be granted the hospital and have it incorporated into their order. However, being excessively favorable to the said preceptor and brothers of the house of Saint Mary of the Germans, and with the said master present at the Apostolic See, they granted the hospital to the aforesaid order, de facto, with the truth of the matters not recognized, despite a legitimate appeal to the Apostolic See by some brothers of the same hospital. Although the said master and brothers of the hospital obtained our letters to the archdeacons of Corinth and Argolis and Master Th., our subdeacon, canon of Coron, no action has yet been taken due to the absence of two judges residing in parts of Italy. They, therefore, humbly requested us to address these grievances with paternal care. We, therefore, command that, if it is so, you restore the said master and brothers to the possession of the hospital and the goods belonging to it, removing any unlawful holders by our authority, and ensure they receive due satisfaction for the fruits taken during the dispossession; restraining those who oppose [etc., up to:] and, having made restitution, if the said preceptor and brothers of Saint Mary of the Germans claim any right in the hospital and wish to dispute it, set a peremptory and suitable term for them to present themselves before us, to do and receive what the order of reason dictates. And if it is established to you about such laying on of hands and imprisonment, proclaim publicly the excommunication of those who committed such sacrilege, and ensure they are strictly avoided by all, until they have adequately satisfied the injured party, etc., up to: absolving. Given at Anagni, the 13th day before the calends of September, in the thirteenth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Papa (Gregorius IX) Magistro Bernardo, subdiacono nostro, canonico Patracensi, mandat ut magistrum et fratres hospitalis Sancti Jacobi de Andrevilla in possessionem hospitalis et bonorum reducat, amotis illicitis detentoribus, et satisfactio de fructibus perceptis exhibeatur; contradictores compescat; et si preceptor et fratres Sancte Marie Teutonicorum jus aliquod in hospitali proponant, terminum peremptorium ad se repraesentandum constituat; si sacrilegium commissum sit, excommunicationem nuntiet. Dat. Anagnie, XIII kalendas septembris, anno tertiodecimo.

He also requests the restitution of the revenues of the said church, which the said archdeacon received from offerings, lands, tithes, and two mills of the same church; all of which he estimates at eighty marks sterling. He also requests that the church of Buckingham, with all its appurtenances and fruits received therefrom, be restored to him, which he says pertains to the said subdeacon by reason of the prebend of Walton, which he holds in the church of Lincoln, and which, he says, pertains by the authority, ordinance, and assent of the chapter of Lincoln and by the will and assent of Blessed Hugh, bishop of Lincoln. To the elected bishop of Liège. From the report of the greater and sounder part of the convent of the monastery of St. James in Liège, of the Order of St. Benedict, we have learned that, although the monastery itself was once troubled by various disputes on account of the less than canonically celebrated election of J., who claims to be its abbot, and although this election was annulled by the authority of our beloved son Otto, cardinal deacon of St. Nicholas in Carcere Tulliano, then legate of the Apostolic See in those parts, due to the defect of the election as well as of the elected: the same person, perjured, simoniac, and entangled in many other crimes, audaciously and ambitiously obtained the governance of the monastery, giving a divorce to virtues and contracting vices, so that he could be called not a monk but demonic, as he presumes to openly keep a concubine, with whom he has fathered two daughters. Claiming to have been dispensed by apostolic authority on this matter, having cast away all monastic modesty and let loose the reins of public incontinence, he presumes to squander the goods of the said monastery, converting them to illicit uses and not observing nor making his subjects observe the regular institutes. Because of this, the monastery has collapsed grievously, both spiritually and temporally, so much so that, unless it is quickly assisted by the providence of the Apostolic See, it will scarcely be able to rise again. Therefore, we were humbly entreated to provide paternal care concerning this matter. Not wishing to let these things pass uncorrected, if they be true, lest another's fault become ours by neglect, we, by apostolic writings, command your discretion, in which we fully trust in God, that you, personally going to the place and having before your eyes only God, rescind any sentence of excommunication found promulgated by the said abbot against A. and W., monks of the said monastery, or others adhering to them, after the said A. and W. undertook the journey to present themselves to us, and that you correct and reform there both head and members, whatever you know to need the duty of correction and reformation. You shall do so with two or three monks prosecuting this business, making sure the necessary expenses are supplied from the goods of the aforesaid monastery. And if you consider J. should be removed from the administration of that monastery, enjoin the convent to provide for themselves a new abbot through canonical election, within a term you shall establish, otherwise you shall yourself provide them with a suitable person. To those contradicting, etc. Given at Anagni, on the third day before the Nones of August, in the thirteenth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX electo Leodiensi mandat ut personaliter loco accedens, ad normam correctionis et reformationis, in capite et membris monasterii Sancti Jacobi Leodiensis, ordinis sancti Benedicti, corrigat et reformet quae indigent, postquam electio abbatis J. minus canonice facta est cassata. Si necesse sit, injungat conventui ut de abbate canonice eligant, alioquin ipse provideat. Dat. Anagnie, III nonas augusti, anno tertiodecimo.

To Olttonil, Cardinal Deacon of St. Nicholas in Carcere Tulliano, legate of the Apostolic See. In the balance of justice. Truly, to our beloved sons, Master Robert of Gloucester and Berard, procurators of our venerable brother, the Archbishop of Canterbury, and Reginald, procurator of Master William of Carney, of the Rochester diocese, constituted at the Apostolic See, we have appointed our beloved son, Thomas, Cardinal Priest of the title of St. Sabina, as auditor. The said Master Robert presented before the auditor that, since the church of Heyneforth had been conferred upon him by the authority of the Apostolic See through the abbot of Boxley, and he had been canonically instituted in it, the mentioned archbishop had wrongfully conferred the same church to the aforementioned William and had invested him in it, to Robert's injury and grievance. Therefore, he sought that the aforementioned process be revoked and that both the one who was so invested and the one investing should be condemned to restore both the aforementioned church and the fruits received from it, as well as to make legitimate satisfaction for damages. However, the opposing procurators lawfully contested the suit before him. Then, after witnesses had been produced and testimonies published, the procurator of the aforementioned William, wishing to return to his own affairs, appointed the aforementioned Berard to see to the remainder of the case and especially to hear the sentence. Finally, after multiple allegations and considerable discussion, the said auditor faithfully recited before us and our brothers what had been proposed on both sides. Therefore, having diligently heard and fully understood the reasons of the parties and having discussed them with careful examination, we deemed it proper to entrust the rendering of our judgment to the aforementioned cardinal. He, by our special mandate and with the counsel of our brothers, declared the process of the aforementioned archbishop and whatever followed from it or because of it null and void, since it was attempted after the grant made by a delegate of the Apostolic See to the said Master Robert and not annulled by law, given that it could not be nullified by the ordinary who was undoubtedly inferior to the delegate in this matter; however, since the abbot had proceeded less cautiously and his grant was found to lack the force of justice, he absolved the opposite party from the claim of the said Master Robert regarding the restitution of fruits and expenses and satisfaction of damages, under the compulsion of justice. Moreover, since, as asserted by many worthy of belief, the merit of life pleads for the said master, and the aid of learning entreats, we mandate that, if the aforementioned William possesses or any other holder after the aforementioned grant of the abbot, is removed from the named church, you confer it with its appurtenances to the said Master Robert by our authority, removing any delay, and ensure that he enjoys peaceful possession, notwithstanding any letters or indulgence obtained from the Apostolic See regarding the mentioned church. If, by chance, it is proven that anyone else had a right in it before the abbot proceeded, to prevent the said master, worn out by labors and exhausted by expenses, from being further oppressed by the repetition of the journey and the impropriety of poverty, by the authority of this present writing, we strictly command you to provide him with at least an equivalent benefice, without appeal. Contradictors etc. Witnesses etc. We firmly forbid any innovation regarding the aforementioned church while the case is pending, decreeing null and void anything attempted against the tenor of our mandate. Given at the Lateran, 14th kalends of June, in the 13th year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Papa Honorius III Olttonili, Sancti Nicolai in Carcere Tulliano diacono cardinali, Apostolicae Sedis legato, mandat ut memorato Willelmo a possessione ecclesiae de Heyneforth post abbatem Boxleyae conferendam amoto, ipsam cum pertinentiis Roberto de Gloucestria, cui per delegatum Apostolicae Sedis iam collata est, restituat, nullis litteris obstantibus; sin autem, alio jus habente, provideat Roberto in equivalenti beneficio. Dat. Laterani, XIIII kalendas Junii, anno pontificatus nostri tertiodecimo.

He, diligently adhering to our instructions, sent us his letters, stating that you had shown him the place called Hackington, sufficiently suitable for this purpose, and your manor of Maidstone, which the legate considered more appropriate for this purpose. However, since a decision was made long ago by the late bishop of Ely and his colleagues, in whom your predecessor and the said prior and convent had compromised, that Canterbury archbishops should not establish a congregation of secular clerics or endow it with the goods of the Canterbury church without the assent of the convent or its major and wiser part, and this decision was accepted by both parties, and Pope Innocent of happy memory, our predecessor, confirmed it, imposing perpetual silence on the parties and their successors regarding the issues settled therein, reserving only to the Canterbury archbishops the ability to establish a certain number of regular persons in the church of Lambeth, if they wished, and assign them certain revenues, expressly prohibiting any congregation of secular canons from being established by them, which might diminish the rights and dignities of the Canterbury church and disturb the holy contemplation therein, such a question should not be resurrected by apostolic concession, having been solemnly resolved with the passage of a long time and expenses. Moreover, since former Canterbury archbishops have endowed so many pious places from the goods of the Canterbury church that they already exceed the amount prescribed by the canons, and the church itself is burdened with so many debts, pensions, and other obligations, to such an extent that it is hardly sufficient for the support of those serving the Lord therein, hospitality, and other burdens, permission should not in any way be granted for you to establish the said college and endow it with the aforementioned revenues and benefices, as it could not be done without significant prejudice to them, because if each of your successors were to apply this, few or little would remain to the church in a short time. To the bishop of Porto, legate of the Apostolic See. Our beloved son, Raymond Bernard, prior of Manso, has shown us by complaint that, although our venerable brothers, the bishop of Tournai, then legate of the Apostolic See in those parts, and afterwards the bishop of Angoulême, and their colleagues and subdelegates, had assigned to him a certain provision in various places of the cities and dioceses of Clermont, Bordeaux, Bazas, and Agen by our authority, although not completely, and certain executors over this matter had been appointed by them and conservators by us: the abbot of Condom violently expelled the said prior from the possession of the goods in the priory of Causdrot, diocese of Bazas, which had been provided to him by the aforesaid authority, causing him other serious harm and injuries. Moreover, the abbots of Aurillac and Sarlat and their convents, as well as the priors of Saint Caprasius, Saint Sacerdos, and Porto, and certain others from the same cities and dioceses, have refused to render to him the provision assigned to him in their monasteries and priories, and have not allowed him to receive the goods granted to him: wherefore diverse sentences of excommunication have been reasonably pronounced against them by the aforesaid bishops and conservators and their subdelegates; some of them, however, for five years and more, have contemptuously ignored these sentences, in peril of their souls, daring to celebrate divine offices under the pretext of certain letters which they are said to have obtained from us in common form, concealing the truth. Furthermore, Amalvinus of Blancafort, a cleric of the diocese of Agen, presumes to withhold part of the provision made to the said prior in the aforesaid priory of Saint Sacerdos by violence, to his prejudice, contemning the sentences of excommunication pronounced against his disturbers by the said executors. But, since it is unworthy for a man of such merit to be oppressed by such vexations, we command you, after inquiring about the aforesaid matters plainly and without judicial clamor, to compel, if it is found to be so, the said abbots and priors and their convents and others, to pay the said provision to him, and to allow him to receive it without difficulty, and to restore what has been withheld, and to make fitting satisfaction for the damages and injuries inflicted, and the expenses he has incurred because of this, by ecclesiastical censure, after prior monition, with appeal removed, punishing them, nevertheless, with canonical penalty for celebrating divine offices while excommunicated. Furthermore, since the said prior, who is known to have endured many labors and irreparable losses for the cause of peace and faith, by himself and his supporters, can scarcely bear the imminent burdens of expenses and scarcely ever be released from the weight of debts contracted because of this, we by the authority of these presents command you to make him enjoy peacefully the receipt of the aforesaid provision, and to supply in the aforesaid cities or dioceses what is lacking to him from this provision, according to the tenor of our mandate, and even to increase it in some of the churches or monasteries and their appurtenances under your legation, even if they belong to the Cluniac order, as you see fit, considering his merits; so that, by our favor, he may rejoice in having received comfort in his many straits, and may bring about an increase of devotion for himself and his supporters towards the Apostolic See. The opposing parties, notwithstanding any indulgence granted to the aforesaid churches and monasteries, even if it is stated that letters obtained may not be valid unless express mention is made of them or their order, and the constitution made in the general council concerning two days, provided that none are drawn beyond the fifth or sixth, and letters obtained from the Apostolic See or even to be obtained, which do not make full mention of the aforesaid. Given at Anagni, on the second Ides of September, in the thirteenth year (of our pontificate).

Gregorius IX episcopo Portuensi, Apostolicae Sedis legato mandat, ut querimoniam dilecti filii Raymundi Bernardi, prioris de Manso, audiat et inquisita veritate compellat abbates et priores, qui provisiones eidem assignatas detinent, ad restitutionem et satisfactionem per censuram ecclesiasticam, necnon puniat eos qui, excommunicati, divina celebrare praesumpserunt. Praeterea, quia prior expensas gravaminaque sustinet, auctoritate pontificia eidem provisionem augeat in civitatibus vel diocesibus sub legation

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop of Lund. Commending your prudence manifoldly, because you seek to be educated by the oracle of the Apostolic See on doubtful matters, we have deemed it necessary to respond to your inquiry. When, as you assert, we directed our writings under a certain form concerning the dispensation of illegitimately born clerics in your province, regarding those clerics who, although at some point they have been concubinarians like their parents, yet having cast aside their concubines before receiving from you the apostolic letters, have begun to perform or completed the penance enjoined upon them, you may dispense them by the authority of this mandate. However, for those who had not yet cast aside their concubines at the time of receiving those letters, the mandate does not grant you the authority to dispense. Nevertheless, wishing to confer a special grace upon you, we grant your fraternity the authority by these presents to dispense with those who have corrected themselves up until these times, following the prescribed form.

Moreover, although concubinarians who return to their concubines after the sentence of excommunication pronounced upon them are bound by the bond of greater excommunication due to their continued crime, other clerics who presumptuously sleep knowingly with those so bound are not bound by the sentence of greater excommunication. Furthermore, if the wooden roofs and structures of churches are entirely destroyed by fire, yet the walls remain intact and the altar table remains in its place, and even if the walls have been stripped of their covering, the church should not be reconsecrated solely due to these reasons, even if the aforementioned roofs and buildings are newly repaired.

The salary that laypeople, with the approval of prelates, set to be paid to the ministers of bishops for their labor during church dedications, since they could not lawfully establish such a thing, cannot be exacted from or received from these laypeople without the stain of simony. Clerics wishing to be promoted to orders, who, distrusting their own knowledge, contract secretly with learned clerics to whisper to their ears what they should respond to during examinations, should be removed from the orders thus received; and those receiving such gifts are to be suspended until they merit obtaining grace concerning this matter.

When an examiner teaches clerics, who due to lack of knowledge are unworthy of ordination, how to respond sophistically without any payment, promise, or retention, so they may be deemed worthy of orders, the same examiner is to be severely punished concerning this until he merits obtaining grace; and clerics thus promoted should be removed from the orders thus received. A priest whom all the parishioners unanimously desire to serve a certain parish church to avoid approaching the bishop due to the arduousness of time and travel, if, with the consent remaining among all, only two of them, hired for their labor and work, pay or promise any money to convey the will of others to the bishop, does not commit the sin of simony. 

To this, the metropolitan at the coronation of a king, in the blessings of abbots or royal marriages, or in the celebration of masses, on a day other than what is expressed in the privilege of his church, should by no means use the pallium; however, we grant your fraternity that if it happens you are to crown the king, you may use the pallium on that day, provided evident utility or necessity requires it. Likewise, one who has begun to perform penance for a mortal sin committed secretly, if that sin later becomes public, must still be enjoined with public penance, and his secret penance should not be considered sufficient based on the testimony of a priest alone.

Given at Anagni, on the ninth day before the Kalends of September, in the thirteenth year.

**Regesto:**

Gregorius Papa IX archiepiscopo Lundensi, super dispensatione clericorum illegitime genitorum instruit, auctoritatem largitur ut cum correctis dispenset, et de reformatione ecclesiarum incendiis laesarum, necnon de clericorum promotionibus et aliis disciplinis ecclesiasticis, praescribit; indulgentiam concedit ut die coronationis regis pallio uti possit. Dat. Anagnie, VIIII kalendas septembris, anno tertiodecimo pontificatus sui.

To Oftonius, deacon cardinal of St. Nicholas in Carcere Tulliano, legate of the Apostolic See. The church of Durham having long been deprived of the solace of a pastor, and our dearest son in Christ, the illustrious king of England, having requested and obtained the customary license to elect, the convent of the same church, having gathered together and invoked the grace of the Holy Spirit, elected their beloved son T., their prior, as bishop. When the king refused to give his assent to this election, despite being humbly requested multiple times, they petitioned our venerable brother, the Archbishop of York, the metropolitan of the place, to confirm the election. However, the king's procurators objected before the archbishop, among other things, that the said prior was a capital enemy of the king, a simoniac, and suspected due to an oath of fealty he had given to our dearest son in Christ, the illustrious king of Scotland. Therefore, they argued that the confirmation of this election should not proceed, as it could cause harm to the king and his kingdom. The archbishop, having accepted the objections regarding simony and enmity, denied the king further audience on all other matters except for the issue of enmity, and later refused to allow the king’s procurators to provide proof, proceeding on his own authority. The king appealed to our audience. Meanwhile, the other party obtained letters from us under certain conditions addressed to the archbishop, and you were instructed that if the archbishop neglected our mandate, you should then proceed in the matter according to the form given to him. The king, objecting that those letters did not mention the previous appeal, contended that they were invalid due to this omission. Since the archbishop refused to provide a copy of these letters when requested, the king also appealed to us. For the king, additional letters were obtained from us addressed to our venerable brother, the Bishop of Lincoln, and his colleagues. However, since you had already begun to examine the case and later referred it back to the Apostolic See, and the Bishop of Lincoln was newly suspected by the king, without whom his colleagues could not proceed, the king did not use these letters, and procurators from both parties went to the Apostolic See. The king requested that we appoint some to proceed in the matter according to the letters obtained for the Bishop of Lincoln and his co-judges, allowing more time for the king to prove the exceptions of enmity and simony, which we had permitted him to present within two months. The opposing party argued that the king's appeals were not to be heard nor pursued, as the legitimate period had already elapsed, and it could not benefit the king if he had indeed sent procurators to the Apostolic See within this time, as he had constrained himself from effectively pursuing his appeals. Additionally, since he had delayed using the letters he obtained, despite having access to the judges, it was presumed to be due to negligence or deceit. The king responded that his procurators were sent to us in due time to pursue the appeals, and letters were obtained for the Bishop of Lincoln and his colleagues, but since the Bishop became suspected by the king, he had rightly not used those letters, as previously stated, which should not prejudice him. We, having understood these matters and others the parties wished to propose, and wishing to prevent dangers to the church of Durham, which might incur significant spiritual and temporal losses due to the lengthy delay of the case, have decided with the counsel of our brothers that the prior should personally present himself at the Apostolic See, and if found sufficient, the king should be silenced regarding these exceptions, and we shall proceed in these and other matters according to our office as we see fit. Therefore, we command you to summon the prior, by our authority, to personally appear before us within a suitable period to be determined by you. Given at Anagni, the third of the nones of October, in the thirteenth year [of our pontificate].

To the same. The beloved son, Rlaymundus Bernardi, prior of Manso, humbly presented before us that the noble man, the count of Toulouse, had unjustly dispossessed him and his church of the villa of Manso, along with the secular jurisdiction and full rights belonging to the said church, as well as other properties. He had extorted an oath of fealty from the men of the said villa. Eventually, the mentioned prior, through the decans of Saint Andrew and Saint Severinus in Bordeaux, was restored to all of the aforementioned, by apostolic authority, with a sentence passed after examining the merits of the case. Furthermore, he was awarded what had been received in the meantime or could have been received, so that he might be adequately compensated for the expenses he incurred, as well as for the damages and injuries inflicted. Because the said count stubbornly refused to comply with the sentence, he, through himself and his seneschal William Arnaldi of Agen, harassed the prior more harshly than usual. They initially pronounced sentences of excommunication against them and, as the count's manifest contumacy grew, they issued sentences of interdict upon his land and any place he might come, by our authority, as justice required. Later on, when we ordered these sentences to be observed inviolably until proper satisfaction was given, they were rightly observed due to the obstinacy of the said count. However, our venerable brother, the bishop of Sorano, then the Apostolic See's legate in those parts, preferring will to reason, without consulting the said prior, improperly lifted these sentences without any satisfaction offered, causing significant harm to him and the mentioned church. Moreover, upon hearing that he was approaching our presence, and provoked by the claim that no procuration was paid to him from the said church of Manso, he unjustly pronounced a sentence of excommunication against the prior, who had not been summoned concerning this issue. But since the prior, driven by the disgrace of poverty and the hardships of exile, was neither bound nor able to pay the procuration, as it is known that he had been dispossessed of the church by the aforesaid count, we, moved by fatherly compassion for him, who suffers for the sake of ecclesiastical liberty, command that, having investigated the above in a straightforward manner without the noise of judicial proceedings, if it is found to be true, you declare the said sentence not to be valid, and unless the said count, with his land and seneschal, fully satisfy the prior and his church for the above within a suitable term that you shall appoint, you are to reinstate the previous sentences and ensure they are reasonably observed, as explained above, until the end. Given at Anagni, on the second Ides of September, in the thirteenth year.

To the bishop, dean, and Martin Perci, canon of Tyrasontum. Our beloved son, the abbot of the monastery of Saint Savior of Leger, of the Cistercian order, in the diocese of Pamplona, showed by petition that, since it was known that the monastery, then of the order of Saint Benedict, collapsed in spiritual and temporal matters, could not be reformed in its own order, we decided to entrust the correction and reformation of it to the Cistercian order, to our venerable brother, the bishop of Pamplona, and his colleagues. J., then prior, and some other monks of the said monastery, appealing in vain to the Apostolic See, the said visitors, considering the appeal frivolous, pronounced a sentence of excommunication, as justice demanded, against them and any other monks of the same monastery who would offer them aid or favor in this. Having ignored this, the aforementioned monks and some others, their supporters, who had previously consented to the reformation of the monastery, presuming to celebrate divine offices, and with the matters presented before our beloved son Cardinal Riccardo of San Angelo, whom we appointed as auditor for the parties then present at the Apostolic See, and faithfully reported to us by him, we directed a letter to our venerable brother, the bishop of Oloron, and his colleagues, instructing them, notwithstanding certain exceptions, to personally visit the monastery if possible, otherwise a suitable place, and having solely God before their eyes, to correct and reform in the said monastery, both in leadership and membership, those things they recognized as needing correction and reformation; and if the said monastery could not be reformed in its order, they were to endeavor to introduce the Cistercian order into it, placing monks of the monastery who did not wish to accept the institutes of this order in some of its parts, invoking secular arm assistance if necessary, and restraining opposers, etc. But, proceeding in the matter according to the form given to them, the aforementioned monks, who acted as the community, asserting to us that they wished to obey the correction and reformation to be made therein by them, obtained from them our letters regarding the relaxation of the previously mentioned sentence of excommunication. Which at length relaxed by the said bishop of Oloron and his colleagues, having received an oath from the monks according to the form of the apostolic rescript, they proceeded in the office of correction and reformation and, considering that, due to the malice of the inhabitants of the aforementioned monastery, it could not be reformed in its order, they introduced by definitive sentence the aforementioned Cistercian order, having consulted prudent and religious men and others, after removing the then abbot. But the oft-mentioned monks, still persisting in their obstinacy of wickedness, refusing to obey that sentence and attempting to weaken their process, despite the contempt of the obligation of the oath, futilely resorted again to an appeal; for which the visitors, not admitting such an appeal, pronounced a sentence of excommunication against them. And although these monks had decided to present themselves before us personally or through a suitable procurator to pursue this appeal on the feast of Blessed John the Baptist, they neither personally nor through any procurator bothered to appear in our presence, as was clearly established from the report of the aforementioned auditor and the visitors' previous process. Therefore, lest the condemnable stubbornness of the aforementioned monks frustrate the reformation made in the monastery itself, we strictly order that, notwithstanding the aforementioned appeal, which they did not prosecute within the set term, you compel the monks to comply with the reformation and ordination of the said bishop of Oloron and his colleagues by making the definitive sentences and sentences of excommunication, until suitable satisfaction, be observed inviolably by ecclesiastical censure, the appeal being set aside, invoking secular arm assistance if necessary; administering our mandate in such a manner that you cannot be accused of negligence or contempt, but rather be commended for your diligence and application. Given at Anagni, 17th day before the calends of October, in the thirteenth year.

Moreover, attempting to seize the lordship of the city of Reims from him, they appointed certain individuals there to hear and decide cases pertaining to his temporal jurisdiction; and, since the gates of the city of Reims belong to his domain and jurisdiction, they had them closed and guarded by armed men, denying free exit to both clerics and others, and, when warned and requested on his behalf to cease such guarding and closure of the gates, they refused. Not content with these actions, as though they were not sufficient offenses, they attempted to construct barbicans, barriers, and a cart to bring a wooden bridge to attack a certain house of his, called the Gate of Mars, and other wooden structures higher than that house, preparing crossbows, quarrels, and other kinds of arms to his detriment and injury, gathering in the same city eighty crossbowmen whose banners they publicly displayed from windows in the market of Reims. To the abbot of Saint Lupus and Master Stephen of Senontis, canon of Troyes. Once, the church of Valence was so burdened with debts, incurred for the defense of its liberty, that it could scarcely rise by its own means. Compassionately, we commanded a tithe of ecclesiastical revenues to be assigned for its aid, for five years in the province of Vienne, and for one year in the province of Lyon and the territory entrusted to the legation of our venerable brother, the bishop of Tournai, legate of the Apostolic See. Although the church gained little benefit from this, so that it might not entirely fail under the weight of debt, we subsequently provided for a moderate subsidy of ten thousand Tours pounds in the aforementioned provinces and territory, with our venerable brother, the archbishop of Vienne, at that time legate of the Apostolic See, appointed as executor. The same archbishop, according to our mandate, carefully assessing the faculties of each diocese, imposed the burden of this subsidy, after prior taxation, on each one as he saw each diocese more or less abundant in its resources, instructing the archbishops and bishops of those dioceses to divide that taxation among themselves and their subordinate churches according to their means. Against this order, our venerable brothers, the archbishop of Narbonne, for himself and some of his suffragans, and the bishops of Maguelone, Autun, Langres, Albi, and Rodez, for themselves and their subjects, appealed to our hearing. Not heeding their appeal, as it was against our mandate, the executor pronounced a sentence of excommunication against them. Eventually, with the procurators of the parties present at the Apostolic See, we decided that, with the aforementioned matters released as a precaution by our beloved son, the abbot of Cluny, according to the form of the Church, two thousand of the ten thousand pounds should be remitted to all, provided that they willingly pay eight thousand, and that those who did not appeal or did not care to pursue their appeal, fully compensate those who pursued their appeal for the expenses they incurred due to this appeal; otherwise, they would not benefit from the aforementioned remission, but that remission would be proportionally made only to those who pursued the issued appeal. The remaining eight thousand Tours pounds should be carefully and faithfully divided among the aforementioned churches by the same abbot, after diligently assessing the faculties of each one, and paid within three years from receipt of our letters, to the church of Valence, so that the money is entirely converted into the payment of debts through the hands of the said abbot. However, because, as the procurator of the church of Valence stated in our presence, it suffered severe damages and expenses due to this subsidy, we, compassionately in the Lord's love towards this church, which almost perishes under the burden of debts, whose revenues scarcely suffice the abyss of usury, we absolutely desire it to be aided according to the taxation we had made, as deemed expedient after diligently inquiring into the faculties of the churches; a sentence of excommunication was issued by our beloved son, Stephen, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Mary in Trastevere, by our special mandate and the advice of our brothers, upon each of those who, according to the amount that affects them, do not provide this subsidy at the next fair in Lagny.
