**Gregorius IX** venerabili fratri .. episcopo, loci diocesano, mandat ut, neglecto illicitio juramento a conventu Latiniacensi extorto, in negotio debitorum auctoritate papali, iuxta priorum litterarum formam, absque appellatione procedat. Monachos vero ad diversa monasteria pro alleviandis debitis missos, donec monasterium onere liberetur, ibidem remanere ac benigne tractari curet; necnon abbates ad retinendum eos per censuram ecclesiasticam compellat. 

Data Laterani, XVI kalendas Februarii, anno septimo.

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop of Tours. Concerning the matter of the election made of our beloved son, Master P., archdeacon of Château-Renault, in the Church of Bourges, which was entrusted to you by us, we have ordered that an inquiry be made by you into certain charges that were brought against him. Having received the inquiry that you sent to the Apostolic See, we entrusted it to our beloved son Efgidius, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian, who faithfully reported everything back to us. Therefore, we command that you carefully and diligently urge the same archdeacon to resign; and if he does not care to comply within the span of one month after your admonition, you shall not delay in annulling his election, instructing the chapter of Bourges to provide for itself through a canonical election of a suitable person as pastor. Given at Rieti, on the twelfth day before the Kalends of July, in the eighth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX archiepiscopo Turonensi mandat ut magistrum P., archidiaconum Castri Radulfi in ecclesia Bituricensi electum, de officio cedere hortetur; qui si infra mensem non obtemperaverit, electionem irritet, monens capitulum Bituricense ut de persona idonea provideat. Datum Reate, XII kalendas julii, anno pontificatus octavo.

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop of Rouen and the Bishop of Coutances,

From your report, along with those of our venerable brother, the Bishop of Avranches, and the nobleman Fulco Paganelli, patron of the monastery of Hambye in the diocese of Coutances, it has come to our attention that although this monastery was constructed by the ancestors of the said nobleman in a pleasant place suitable for religion and richly endowed, so that, with the Lord's name invoked, both they and their posterity might be aided by the prayers and merits of those living religiously there, the situation has sadly deteriorated contrary to what was hoped for. For the black monks of said monastery have become darkened both outwardly and inwardly, serving not God but the devil, being proprietors, dissolute, marked by the lures of the flesh, and showing almost no sign of regular observance. They indulge in feasting and drinking, roam separately through chambers, and move about in pairs or threesomes like lowly laymen in taverns, impiously misusing the things granted for pious uses, to the extent that the resources, which could support sixty Cistercian brothers, seem insufficient for them, numbering twenty-six. Therefore, as you claim, despite your long efforts, brother Bishop of Coutances, who are their diocesan, and those of the abbot of the place, to correct them—who are now not monks but demons—and with the Ethiopian not changing his skin or the leopard his spots, they have become utterly incorrigible. Therefore, since there seems to be no other remedy whereby the place might be reformed into a proper order, we command by the authority of these presents that, if it is so, you expel the bad husbandmen from the vineyard of the Lord and introduce into the aforementioned monastery a convent of the Cistercian order, who will yield fruit to God in due time. Take care to place any of the aforementioned who refuse to accept the institutes of the said order into other monasteries of their religion. Opponents etc. Given at Rieti, on the 17th day before the calends of July, in the eighth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX archiepiscopo Rothomagensi et episcopo Constantiensi mandat ut, monachis monasterii de Hambeia propter incorrigibilitatem eiectis, conventum Ordinis Cisterciensis inducant. Dat. Reate, XVII kalendas julii, anno octavo.

**Translation to English:**

To the bishop, master Peter, the official of the people of Troyes, and the archdeacon of Sens. By the report of our beloved sons, the abbot and convent of the monastery of Saint Peter of Celle, in the diocese of Troyes, you should know that we have learned that, when they previously opposed Stephen of Camp-Guidonis, a citizen of Troyes, for having rashly built a chapel in his grange of Chiceriacum, situated in the parish of Saint Andrew near the named monastery, without seeking their consent, thus coming against the tenor of their privileges, they brought the matter before the abbot of Saint James of Provins and his colleagues with apostolic authority. They requested that what had been thus built be demolished, and that certain women, intruded there under monastic habit on their own authority, be removed, as they were not to hear divine services there. Finally, the case was referred back to us, and we appointed our beloved son Stinibaldus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Lawrence in Lucina, as judge along with John, their proctor, and Jacfobol, the proctor of those women, with none appearing for the aforementioned citizen. When the matter was litigated for some time before him by the said proctors, it was judged by the same that, for the reasons contained in their petition, such a construction should not be destroyed, absolving the opposing party entirely from their accusations concerning those matters. Therefore, they humbly asked us that, since those aforementioned women are placed in that chapel, which is so close to their monastery that the voices of those singing psalms can be heard from there, who profess the Cistercian order by word but do not observe it in deed, since they are neither incorporated into it nor reside continuously in the cloister, but rather frequently wander through various places—by whose proximity their monastery, which was previously of great repute, is very much defamed, and it is feared that it might be entirely destroyed on account of this proximity, which gives rise to an evil presumption, nor is their parish right injured, we might deign to provide for them concerning these matters with the benevolence of the Apostolic See, since these issues were not addressed in the prior judgment. Therefore, since, according to the Apostle, our daily concern is the continuous care of all the churches, we command you that, having diligently inquired into all the aforementioned matters, if you find the situation to be so, you should take care to provide such a remedy by our authority regarding this proximity that neither dangers to souls, nor sinister suspicions or scandals may arise from either side, nor the condition or peace of the aforesaid monastery and chapel be disturbed in any way, with the sentence of the aforesaid cardinal enduring in its strength. Given at the Lateran, on the 6th of May, in the eighth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Honorarius III episcopo, magistro Petro, officiali Trecensibus, et archidiacono Senonensi mandat ut, inquisita diligentius veritate circa vicinitatem mulierum non legitime in capella, quae in grangia Chiceriaci edificata est, ad monasterium Sancti Petri de Cella spectante, si rem ita esse invenerint, taliter auctoritate apostolica ordinent ut nec pericula animarum nec scandalum exinde oriatur, sententia cardinalis Stinibaldi in suo robore manente. Datum Laterani, VI Idus Maii, anno octavo.

**Translation to English:**

To the bishop, dean, and archdeacon of Burgos. A petition was presented to us by our beloved sons, the preceptor and brothers of the house of the knights of Monfragüe, which, as it is said, belongs directly to the Roman Church with its appurtenances, without any intermediary. The petition stated that, since their order was founded by the late Raymond I, Count of Galicia, to combat the infidelity of the Saracens in parts of Spain and was eventually confirmed by the Apostolic See, it achieved such growth in prosperity, through divine power, that many benefits accrued to the Christian people. However, the master and brothers of Calatrava, of the Toledo diocese, induced the master and some brothers of the said order by promises and gifts, so that, having abandoned the sign of their own profession, and against the opposition and appeal of the remaining brothers to the Apostolic See, they presumed to take on their habit by their own authority, and to subject themselves and the whole order of Monfragüe along with all the goods acquired by the generosity of the faithful, to the order of Calatrava. Therefore, the said master and brothers of Calatrava unlawfully hold and refuse to return the possessions, castles, houses, and other goods of the said house of Monfragüe, as well as the castle of the said place. They have therefore requested the provision of the Apostolic See to assist them. Wherefore, by the power of obedience, we strictly command you, if this is the case, to return to the aforementioned preceptor and brothers all the above-mentioned things, along with the fruits received in the meantime, as is just, by summoning those who should be summoned and hearing the claims from both sides, to make what is canonical, etc.; and also in the meantime to provide the said preceptor and brothers of Monfragüe with the necessary expenses for themselves and their advocates from the goods of the said house. Notwithstanding the constitution regarding two diets, etc. If not all of you, etc., you, brother bishop, etc. Given at Rieti, on the nones of June, in the eighth year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Papa Honorius III episcopo, decano et archidiacono Burgensibus mandat ut, si ita est, preceptori et fratribus domus militie de Monfrago possessiones, castra et bona ab ordine Calatravensi contra justitiam detenta, cum fructibus perceptis restituantur, vocatis qui fuerint evocandi et auditis propositis; et interim necessarias expensas ministrari jubet. Dat. Reate, nonis junii, anno octavo.

**Translation to English:**

To Brother Jordan, of Saint Benedict of Padua, and .. of Saint Mary of Monte Crucis, priors of the Paduan diocese, and to Master Gabriel of Prato, canon of Aquileia, residing in Padua. Our beloved son Hegno, known as the Count of Epianfol, our subdeacon and canon of Trent, has appeared in our presence and explained that our venerable brother, the Bishop of Trent, conducts sales of victuals and other goods in a certain house, commonly called "cannapa", at lower prices and allows them to be sold at higher prices, and does not permit such trade according to ancient custom elsewhere in the city of Trent. This is to the prejudice and disadvantage of the said canon, as well as to the detriment of the poor and miserable persons, imposing upon him unusual and undue exactions. He has suffered many damages, injuries, and expenses, leading him to appeal to our hearing on this matter. Ignoring his legitimate appeal, the same bishop has pronounced a sentence of excommunication against him, without warning, conviction, or confession, being otherwise very burdensome and injurious to him. We have ordered him to be absolved from this excommunication through Brother Raymond, our penitentiary, after receiving sufficient caution from him that, if it is proven that he was justly bound, he will make satisfaction, as required, for those matters for which he was excommunicated. He has humbly requested that provision be made for him and the aforementioned persons by the Apostolic See regarding other matters. Since we cannot fail to support our subdeacon in his rights, as we are indebted to all in justice, we command that if this is the case, you compel the said bishop to desist entirely from this grievance and illicit gain from the trade, both against him and the aforementioned persons and miserable persons concerning the aforementioned matters, and to make restitution for the injuries and damages incurred, as required. Compel the canon, if it is proven that he was justly excommunicated, to make satisfaction for those matters for which he was bound, as is fitting. Witnesses, etc. If not all, etc. Given at the Lateran, on the 8th day before the Ides of May, in the year ...

**Regesto in Latin:**

Papa [Nomen Papae] mandat Fratri Jordano et Sancti Benedicti Paduani prioribus, necnon Magistro Gabrieli de Prato, canonico Aquilegensi, ut Tridentinum episcopum compellant desinere a gravaminibus et illicito mercimonio contra subdiaconum Hegnonem et pauperes personas. Episcopus Tridentinus excommunicationis sententiam in Hegnonem injuste tulerat; Papa providet ut Hegno absolutionem recipiat, si legitime ligatus fuisset. Datum Laterani, VI idus maii, anno pontificatus [Anno Pontificatus].

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Narni. Although previously, having understood that the abbot and convent of the Monastery of St. Benedict in Fundis, inspired by Him whose spirit breathes where it will, transformed into new men and imitating greater virtues, desired to incorporate themselves and their monastery into the Cistercian Order, and with us assenting to their wishes, had commanded, with your agreement and that of the Narni chapter, that they be incorporated into the aforementioned order, after first making a union with the Monastery of St. Matthew of the Cistercian Order in the Diocese of Rieti, with the abbot and convent of St. Matthew transferring to the said St. Benedict monastery, and the abbot and convent of St. Benedict receiving the habit of the aforementioned order: nevertheless, because for many reasons presented before us this union cannot be preserved, and the same abbot and convent look back, almost yearning for the melons and leeks of Egypt, with you expressly denying that such a union was made with your or your chapter's assent, unless certain compensations were made and conditions imposed, with certain reservations for you and your church regarding the aforementioned St. Benedict monastery, we revoke the union, returning the matter to the state it was known to be in before the union. Therefore, we give orders by our letters to our venerable brother the bishop and beloved son B. Moysi, canon of Rieti, that after they first return the abbot and convent of the Monastery of St. Matthew to their own monastery, they then restore you to the possession, or near possession, of the aforementioned monastery, in which you and your predecessors are known to have been before the said union. As for those who may oppose, etc. Given at the Lateran, on the twelfth kalends of March, in the seventh year (of our pontificate).

**Regesto in Latin:**

Papa Gregorius IX episcopo Narniensi mandat ut, unione inter monasterium Sancti Benedicti in Fundis et ordinem Cisterciensem revocata, abbate et conventu Sancti Mathei ad monasterium proprium reversis, episcopum Narniensem in possessionem monasterii Sancti Benedicti restituat, prout ante unionem fuerat. Dat. Laterani, XII kalendas martii, anno septimo.

**Translation to English:**

To the bishops of Melfi and Minervino. Beloved sons, the abbot and convent of the monastery of Case Dei have shown us through a submitted petition that, a while ago, a dispute arose between the beloved sons, the clergy and people of Monte Peloso on one side, and their monastery on the other, concerning the episcopal dignity, which the clergy and people demanded to be restored to them. Pope Celestine of blessed memory, our predecessor, by a definitive sentence, silenced them on this matter. He wisely decreed that the church of Santa Maria Nova of Monte Peloso, as a priory with all the churches of that place, both inside and outside, should forever be subject spiritually and temporally to the monastery of Case Dei, and that the prior appointed there from time to time by the monastery should invite any bishop he wished once or twice a year to administer the episcopal sacraments to them, as is more fully contained in his authentic document. And although this sentence has been observed until now, it was nullified by Pope Innocent III of blessed memory, our predecessor, due to the presumption concerning a certain person who was unlawfully intruded as their bishop during the interim period. Yet, the said clergy and people oppose this sentence by presuming to act against it, to the considerable detriment of the aforementioned monastery. Therefore, unwilling that what has been wisely established by our predecessors be weakened by any rashness, we have decided to request and exhort their community, giving them a mandate through our letters, to observe that sentence thus, revoking presumptions contrary to it, so that they seem to be retracted from harmful actions not by negligence but by will. Therefore, we command that you ensure this sentence is firmly observed, and that any opponents and rebels, if there are any, be addressed, etc. Provided that the community of Monte Peloso, etc. Given at the Lateran, on the 4th of the Nones of May, in the eighth year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX episcopis Melfiensis et Minerbinensis mandat ut sententiam definitam a predecessoribus suis Celestino et Innocentio III observandam curent, qua ecclesia Sanctae Mariae Novae Montis Pilosi cum ecclesiis subesse debet monasterio Case Dei. Contradictores et rebelles compescant. Data Laterani, die quarta Nonas Maii, anno pontificatus octavo.

**Translation to English:**

To the same persons. Since the case which is between the beloved sons, the preceptor and brothers of the house of the militia of Monfrague, on one side, and the master and brothers of Calatrava of the Toledo diocese, on the other side, concerning the castle of Monfrague and other matters, we have formerly entrusted to you, and you, having legally contested the lawsuit before you, have received witnesses and published depositions, and after a long dispute made from both sides, you have sufficiently instructed the case and sent it to our examination, setting a suitable term for the parties to present themselves before the apostolic presence through suitable procurators to receive the sentence. And since we have granted our beloved son O., the cardinal deacon of St. Nicholas in Carcere Tulliano, as an auditor to the party of the said preceptor and brothers of the house of Monfrague, who appeared before us at the same term, and since no one appeared for the other party, despite having waited for a long time, we have finally, being fully informed about the process of the said case by the same cardinal, seen it fit that it should rather be settled by agreement than by judgment. Therefore, wishing still to defer to the said master and brothers of Calatrava in this part, we strictly command you, by the virtue of obedience, that, having summoned the parties to your presence, you induce them to make a friendly settlement among themselves, to which you should lend prompt and effective assistance as diligently as possible, while also more earnestly admonishing the aforementioned Calatrava brothers on our behalf that, content with their own rights, they should not seek to enrich themselves at the peril of their souls and the detriment of their order by any pretext with the loss of others. But if a friendly settlement cannot be reached between the parties, you shall terminate the case according to the process held before you with a canonical conclusion, meanwhile ensuring that the said preceptor and brothers, etc., as above. Notwithstanding etc. And if not all etc., as above. Given at Rieti, the 2nd day before the Kalends of June.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Papa Gregorius IX eisdem mandat ut causam inter praeceptorem et fratres domus militiae de Monfrague et magistrum ac fratres Calatravenses Toletanae dioecesis super castro de Monfrague componant, partibus ad compositionem amicabilem inducendis vel, si compositione nequiverit, causam fine canonico terminandam. Datum Reate, II kalendas Junii, anno pontificatus sui quinto.

**Translation to English:**

The same [Pope] to the same [recipient]. To the most holy father, etc. Regarding the land beyond the Rhône in the regions of the Empire, which, by your will, we have held and safeguarded in our hand for some time, with deliberation had in our counsel, we recall having previously requested your fatherhood to restore that land to our beloved and faithful kinsman, R., Count of Toulouse, who, along with his predecessors, also possessed that land in times past, confident that through this he might be encouraged to maintain the peace of the Church in those parts and to exhibit more devoted service to us; we are particularly induced to this because the aforementioned count has no heir except for a single daughter, who is to be matrimonially joined, by your dispensation, to our dearest brother. Therefore, we seek this favor as one that will benefit us and ours. Thus, we have deemed it suitable to request your kindness once again to restore the aforementioned land to the said count, hoping for the devotion we expect will follow from this, with the Lord's granting it, considering also that, as we have learned from the testimony of the prelates of those parts, he has been vigilant, faithful, and devoted in seeking out heretics and punishing them, once found, to the honor of God and the Holy Church. Hence, it seems good and beneficial to us and our counsel that such grace be shown to him, so that he may become more devoted to God and the Holy Church from his devotion; we also affectionately ask your fatherhood to kindly and favorably hear the aforementioned count in his other just petitions, for the love of us. Given at Loriacum, on the day after the feast of Saint Gregory.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius Papa IX, ad sanctissimum patrem (recipiens) mandat quatenus terram ultra Rodanum in partibus Imperii, quam cum voluntate ipsius in manu sua tenuerat, restituat dilecto et fideli consanguineo suo, R., comiti Tolosano, qui eam cum antecessoribus suis temporibus retroactis possederat, ut per hoc alliciatur ad pacem Ecclesiae servandam et ad servitium devotius praestandum, cum precipue comes heredem non habeat nisi unicam filiam copulandam fratri suo ex dispensatione papali. Rogat etiam ut comitem in justis petitionibus suis benigne exaudiat. Datum apud Loiriacum, in crastino sancti Gregorii, pontificatus sui anno.

**Translation to English:**

To Master Vernacius, canon of Treviso, residing in Paris. When we previously directed our letters to the dean of St. Martin of Tours, instructing him to freely assign one of the prebends of the same church, which did not have the care of souls attached, to Riccardo, son of the noble man Rainerius de Arsul., canon of the same church, if any were vacant at that time or as soon as an opportunity arose, and the dean objected due to Riccardo's insufficient age, Riccardo obtained various letters from us at different times regarding this matter. Recently, however, the same dean, in order to appear to comply with our mandates in some way, offered him the prebend of Meritiaco, from which the said canon could derive little or almost no benefit, and petitioned insistently to be relieved from paying the pension of twenty pounds, which he was compelled to provide by our mandate until a prebend was provided to him, before our beloved son R., cardinal deacon of St. Mary in Cosmedin, who was appointed as his auditor by us. But since Riccardo did not accept the aforementioned prebend because it seemed not only meager but almost useless, especially since it was located in an unsafe place and access to it was not easy, his father R. humbly petitioned us on his behalf to graciously continue our favor towards him. Therefore, wishing that the said canon may achieve in effect what he is known to have hoped from us, we command that you confer and assign to the said canon another prebend, if any presently vacant in the aforementioned church, worth at least fifty pounds of Tours currency, by our authority; otherwise, reserve the first one to become vacant of the same value for our donation, to be conferred by you to him, declaring null and void any attempt otherwise concerning it. Any opposing parties, etc. Meanwhile, compel the dean to pay him an annual pension of twenty-five pounds of the same currency. Notwithstanding any letters obtained from the Apostolic See and the constitution concerning the two diets, etc. Given at Rieti, 17th of the Kalends of July, in the eighth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Papa Honorius III, Magistro Vernacio, canonico Tervisino, Parisiis commoranti, mandat ut unam preposituram in ecclesia Sancti Martini Turonensis vacantem, valorem ad minus quinquaginta librarum Turonensis monete, Riccardo, filio Rainerii de Arsul., canonicus ejusdem ecclesiae, auctoritate sua conferat et assignet; alioquin primo vacaturam ejusdem valoris donationi suae reservet. Interea decanum compellat ut ei annuam pensionem viginti quinque librarum solvat. Dat. Reate, XVII kalendas Julii, anno pontificatus octavo.

**Translation to English:**

To Cesarius, our beloved son J., cardinal priest of the title of St. Praxedis, vicar in the March of Ancona. Since our beloved son Egidius, to whom we deemed it fit to entrust the care of the Farfa monastery and its dependencies, suspended Henry, then abbot of the same monastery, who was considered not only useless but even pestilent, from his administration, and among other things beneficially prohibited him from entering the March without our special license, promulgating sentences of excommunication and removal from the administration of spiritual and temporal affairs if he presumed to act contrary: the same Henry, as we have learned, disregarding the aforesaid sentences, presumptuously entered the March and violently attacked the castles of the aforesaid monastery, wickedly usurping the administration of temporal and spiritual affairs, plundering, dissipating, devouring, and consuming the goods of the same monastery and its dependencies. Moreover, forgetful of his own salvation and a scorner of ecclesiastical discipline, he shamelessly intruded into the communion of the faithful, having solemnly, or rather damnably, made divine services celebrated for himself in the churches of the aforesaid monastery, through which he roams, having cast off all reverence. Therefore, wishing to provide with fatherly solicitude for the indemnity of the said monastery, we give our firm precepts by our letters to all monks, clerics, faithful, and vassals of the Farfa monastery established in the March of Ancona, and strictly prohibit them from henceforth rendering any counsel, aid, or favor to the same Henry, whom we decree to be absolved from their obedience and loyalty, lest his deserving temerity be emboldened; otherwise, we will, with the Lord's authority, cause the sentences rightly pronounced or to be pronounced by the same cardinal against the rebellious to be inviolably observed until due satisfaction is rendered. Moreover, we declare all concessions, donations, and liberties made by the aforementioned Henry from the time of his suspension concerning the goods or rights of the said monastery or its dependencies, in whatever way or title to anyone, written or unwritten, to be null and void, so that no prejudice may arise in the future to the monastery and its members; and all mutual contracts presumed by the same Henry up to now or henceforth, in whatever form or manner, shall have no force of validity; to the payment of which we will that the said monastery or its members shall not be held. Therefore, we command that you compel the aforementioned Henry to leave without delay the whole land of the said monastery, using spiritual, and if necessary, added temporal coercion, without appeal, having the tenor of the present letters solemnly published throughout the same land, both by you and by other trustworthy persons, reduced to public documents in every place of the said land through the hands of notaries, lest ignorance be claimed by anyone in the future as a means of defense. Given.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX Cesario, dilecto filio J., tituli Sanctae Praxedis presbytero cardinali, in Marchia Anconitana vicario mandat ut Henricum, abbatem monasterii Farfensis, qui ab administratione suspensus et sententias contemnens, temere in Marchiam ingressus est et bona monasterii depraedatur, de terra monasterii discedere compellat, interdicens fidelibus ne ei assistent, et actus ab eo post suspensionem gestos irritos decernit. Dat. Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To the prior and monks of Santa Maria de Ofida. We have taken upon ourselves the care of governance. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, desiring to provide for your peace, we receive your house and persons, with the castle of Ofida and its appurtenances, and with all that you rightfully possess at present or may justly obtain in the future, with God's favor, under the protection of blessed Peter and our own, following the example of our predecessor, Pope Celestine of happy memory. We especially receive the Church of Saint Angel with the mill; the Church of Saint Angel in Flenga; the Church of Saint John in Colle Lucido; the Church of Saint Martin with its court and appurtenances; the Church of Saint Peter Beveianfil; the Church of Saint Pantaleon; the Church of Saint Giles; the Church of Saint Nicholas; the Church of Saint Emindius; the Church of Saint Angel in Apriniano; the Church of Saint Benedict; the Church of Saint Andrew; the Church of Saint Peter in Cesis; the Church of Saint Mary, priest Azo; the Church of Saint Valentine; the Church of Saint John; the Church of Saint Peter of Ozano; the Church of Saint Venantius; the Church of Saint Angel in Laureto, with all the possessions given to you by Marsilius Alberti; all the churches of Coseniani, Oliani, and Insule, and the donation of Marsilius, son of Trajan, and all, with the appurtenances of the aforementioned churches, which you justly and without controversy possess, we confirm to you and to your church through you by apostolic authority and strengthen by the protection of this present writing. Furthermore, we decree and strictly forbid by apostolic authority that no prior or monk may be admitted or excluded in the said house without the common consent of the brothers or the greater and sounder part. Moreover, since the clerics of your churches receive those churches from you, and also, as you assert, are ordained by catholic bishops with your letters, we grant you by the authority of these presents that, as it exists within the jurisdiction of your monastery, those same clerics shall in future times pertain to your correction, and observe it reverently and humbly according to the gravity of the offense. We further prohibit anyone from daring to pronounce a sentence of suspension, excommunication, or interdict upon you or your church without a manifest and reasonable cause. As a token of this protection received from the Apostolic See, you shall pay us and our successors two bezants annually for said monastery and one for your castle. We therefore decree that it is not lawful for anyone whatsoever. But if anyone, etc. Given at Rieti, on the eighth day before the Ides of June.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius Papa IX priori et monachis Sanctae Mariae de Ofida domum, personas et possessiones eorum, cum castro et omnibus pertinentiis, sub protectione beati Petri et sua suscipit et confirmat auctoritate apostolica, prohibens admissionem vel exclusionem monachorum sine communi consensu et concedens correctionem clericorum suarum ecclesiarum. Prohibet sententias suspensionis, excommunicationis aut interdicti sine causa rationabili. Annua pensio duorum bizantiorum pro monasterio et unius pro castro imponitur. Datum Reate, VI Idus Iunii, pontificatus anno.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Burgos, Master A., elected Bishop of León, and the Dean of Zamora. A beloved son, the abbot of the monastery of San Facundo, presented before us that when the abbots of Spina and Cella Nova, along with Master T., the treasurer and then archdeacon of Palencia, claiming to be appointed as visitors of exempt monasteries in the kingdom of Castile and León by the Apostolic See, came to his monastery intending to execute their office of visitation, the said abbot objected before them, stating that neither his person nor the monastery should or could be visited by them by law. The abbot of Spina was bound by excommunication for violently laying hands on Peter the monk, who was not subject to him; he was also suspicious because although the visitation of exempt monasteries was said to be entrusted to him and his colleagues without specifying his name, he, even though he was not yet an abbot, proceeded with the treasurer to the prejudice and harm of the monastery. The abbot of Cella Nova was bound by an excommunication sentence laid by our venerable brother, the Bishop of Sabina, then the legate of the Apostolic See in those parts, upon all those living in concubinage, into which he fell by maintaining a concubine. The treasurer was suspect to him as he had publicly threatened to remove him from the monastery and had conspired with some of his enemies against him, and was excessively friendly and familiar with some of his enemies, from whose hands he had rescued the town of San Facundo, all of which or individually he offered to prove lawfully before arbitrators to be commonly chosen, which he was ready to choose immediately. And because the aforementioned judges unjustly refused to admit these legitimate exceptions of his, he, though gravely ill, feeling unduly aggrieved, appealed to our hearing. But they, disregarding his legitimate appeal, after inflicting many injuries upon him, removed him from the governance of the monastery by definitive sentence, absolving the monks from obedience and the vassals from their loyalty to him, granting the monks free power of choosing, and pronouncing a sentence of excommunication against him if he continued to act as abbot and against those who favored or supported him. Indeed, we are deeply pained by the fact that, although the Romans ought to be special sons of the Church, they have degenerated from sons into stepsons and have shown themselves so disloyal and ungrateful that it seems little spark of devotion or gratitude remains in them. For their iniquity has so grown, like fat, that they not only stretch out their reckless hands to temporal matters, which do not pertain to them, but also to spiritual matters entirely forbidden to laymen, seeking to utterly overturn and subvert ecclesiastical freedom, and to enslave the Roman Church, their mother, which is the mirror and exemplar of all churches, thereby inciting all against the liberty of the universal Church by the perniciousness of their example. Since, although this offense is grave, yet, because such persecution has lasted so long, the example is graver, we have been compelled by pastoral diligence to bind up what was broken in them, and to restore what was cast away, laboring through earnest admonitions and frequent exhortations. But they were not given from above to receive the saving medicine for their wound, for which we have toiled greatly to heal; and so we have taken care to exercise ecclesiastical censure upon them. And because their iniquities have grown so great that they neither fear God nor respect ecclesiastical censure, we are compelled, though unwillingly, to rouse you and other sons and devoted supporters of the Church, against them for vengeance, affectionately asking and earnestly exhorting your brotherhood, and strictly commanding you through apostolic writings, that prudently considering the nature of the cause at hand, since it is public, not private; not particular, but common, in which you are more strongly bound to rise to our aid, as we intend not to defend a few in particular but all in general, you may provide us with a fitting subsidy of soldiers or mercenaries as liberally and willingly as possible, so that, supported by your and others' aid, we may, with the Lord's help, so repress their impudent pride that others may not in future lift themselves against God and the Church, and that the sons of the Church may rejoice in due freedom. And we, knowing more fully your sincerity from the affection and effect of the liberality shown, may embrace you more dearly in the bowels of Christ. Given at Perugia, on the Nones of December, in the eighth year.

To the archbishops and bishops, abbots, priors, deans, archdeacons, masters of the Hospital and the knighthood of the Temple, and other religious houses, and to all the prelates of churches established throughout the province of Jerusalem. When our venerable brother, the Patriarch of Jerusalem, from the divine disposition of counsel, received from the Apostolic See the power of a dual office over the peoples of the province of Jerusalem, which, due to the sins of the Christian people, have received double from the hand of the Lord, so that, set apart for the Gospel of God, he might exercise not only the honor of patriarchal dignity but also the office of legation. And, by the will of Him who directs the steps of men, his return has been delayed at the Apostolic See, where he has laudably resided until now: we send him back to his church with the same power and fullness of our grace, mandating to all of you that you receive him humbly and devotedly as the legate of the Apostolic See, and that you fully attend to him in all matters as before he came to our presence. Otherwise, we will hold and cause to be observed, with the Lord as our witness, inviolably, any sentence that he may reasonably pass against the rebellious. Given at Interamna, on the 6th day before the Ides of February, in the tenth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX archiepiscopis, episcopis, abbatibus, prioribus, decanis, archidiaconis, magistris Hospitalis et militia Templi, et universis ecclesiarum prelatis in provincia Jerosolimitana mandat ut patriarcham Jerosolimitanum, tanquam legatum Apostolicae Sedis, humiliter recipiant et ei plene in omnibus obediant, alioquin sententias eius contra rebelles ratas habebit. Datum Interamne, VIII idus Februarii, anno decimo.

To the Masters Peter de Sonion, penitentiary of Beauvais, Wernacius of Treviso, and Ricefardo, called Angelo, canons of Le Mans, residing in Paris. We have received a complaint from our beloved son, the abbot of the monastery of Saint Victor in Paris, stating that, although the abbots of Saint Genevieve and some others of his order customarily convened annually at the monastery for a general chapter, and under his presidency, established matters for the reformation of the order, those same abbots have unjustly deprived him of this role. Thus, when the procurators of the parties were present before us, we assigned our beloved son O[tto], cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in Carcere Tulliano, as the auditor; before whom, after a plea was presented by the abbot’s procurator to the opposing party’s procurator, and the matter was legally disputed, because full faith could not be given to what was proposed on either side, we decided to entrust the case to Master Jacob, archdeacon of Morin, and his co-judges under certain conditions, instructing them, nevertheless, to receive an oath of truth from the principal parties. Later, when our beloved sons, abbots of Saint Satyrus in the diocese of Bourges, and Saint Ambrose in the diocese of Bourges, presented themselves, both in person and on behalf of Saint Genevieve of Paris, Saint Evurtius of Orleans, the abbey of Jardo in Sens, Saint Bartholomew of Noyon, the abbey of Aqua Curte in Arras, Saint Vincent of Soissons, and the abbey of Julli in Meaux, and G., a canon of the aforementioned monastery, a procurator of the same abbot, to obtain and oppose a mandate at the Apostolic See, we assigned the same cardinal as the auditor: then, on behalf of themselves and the previously mentioned abbots, they alleged before him that, because two of the aforementioned judges, in the absence and without legitimate excuse of the third, were proceeding unjustly if he was unwilling or unable to participate in the deliberation of the case, they appealed to our audience; but the same judges, disregarding their appeal, which they considered contumacious, issued sentences of suspension and excommunication against them; from which they requested, on behalf of themselves and those abbots, to be absolved as a precaution. However, the aforementioned procurator proposed in opposition that they should not be heard on this matter but should be sent back to the previous judges, from whom they had unjustly departed through the objection of a frivolous appeal, delaying the matter for nearly two years. Therefore, after carefully hearing these matters and what the same cardinal faithfully reported before us, wanting the mentioned matter to reach a proper conclusion swiftly, we, through our brother G., our penitentiary, granted to the abbots of Saint Satyrus and Saint Ambrose the benefit of absolution as a precaution by our mandate, and the sentence of suspension being lifted, we command that you grant the other aforementioned abbots the benefit of absolution as a precaution before proceeding to other matters, and similarly lift the mentioned sentence of suspension. Given at Terni, on the eleventh day before the calends of February, in the tenth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Papa, magistris Petro de Sonion, penitentiario Belvacensi, Wernacio, Tervisino, et Ricefardo dicto Angelo, canonicis Cenomanensibus Parisius commorantibus mandat ut absolutionis beneficium abbatiis Sancti Satiri et Sancti Ambrosii, ceterisque abbatibus provideant, et suspensionis sententiam relaxent. Datum Interamne, XI kalendas februarii, anno decimo.

Also, we cite the Bishop of Riga for preaching, dispensing, absolving, granting indulgences, presuming to make carinal redemptions and exchanging vows throughout Terronia, as if he had apostolic authority, and for giving these plenary faculties to others, since he never had apostolic authority for them. Also, because, as is said, having an uncanonical entry, and having requested resignation from the legate of the Apostolic See, and with the Bishop of Semigallia having been commanded by the apostolic mandate that if he would not resign, he should be sent to the presence of the Lord Pope, yet repenting of this, he neither resigned at the legate’s command nor cared to present himself to the Lord Pope. Also, we cite the entire fraternity of the Knights of Livonia regarding the matter where, at the command of the Lord Cardinal O., then legate of the Apostolic See, they restored the entrusted lands, namely Wironia and Gerva, to B., now Bishop of Semigallia, then serving as vice of the said legate in those parts, in the name of the Roman Church, but subsequently violently seized these lands from the same B. Also, because at the same time they usurped the provinces of Courland, voluntarily converted and received into the hands of the said Church by the same vice-legate, on the pretext of a certain unjust arbitration, with their hosts; subsequently, upon his withdrawal to the Roman Curia, they promoted expeditions through these provinces, devastating them through fires and murders, and finally, they seized the liberty letters of Curonian neophytes, confirmed and endorsed by the seals of the same brothers and prelates from the parts of Livonia by the Lord Pope, reducing the neophytes of those provinces to servitude, generating a grave scandal both to neophytes and to other conversed and to-be-converted pagans. To Master Andrew, our chaplain, residing in Bologna. Our beloved sons, the chapter of Pula, have shown us by their petition that their church is deprived of the solace of a pastor. They elected their archdeacon, while our venerable brother, the Patriarch of Aquileia, elected B., the provost of Concordia, to the governance of the said church. We have instructed our venerable brother, the Bishop of Castellan, and our fellow colleagues by our letters to diligently inquire into the manner of the elections, the intentions of the electors, and the merits of the elected, and to inform us of their findings by their letters. However, when the said provost decided to appeal to our hearing, and the aforementioned judges deferred to his appeal, we, at the instance of the said provost and upon the chapter's supplication to proceed with the case in our presence, have decided to commit the matter to the Abbot of St. Stephen of Bologna and his co-judges, with the instruction to proceed according to the content of the former letters, and to ensure the case is sufficiently prepared and referred back to us; before whom, after the said provost appeared through a procurator and the process had been ongoing for some time, and the judges later cited him personally, the same provost, claiming the place to be unsafe for him, sought refuge in appeal; and since the aforesaid judges, wishing to remove any opportunity for deceit, decided to grant him another secure place, he, using the pretext of the same appeal, maliciously seeks to prolong the matter, to the considerable detriment of the same church, which has already remained without a pastor's governance for over two years. The said chapter has requested that provision be made, especially since the same provost, due to a lack of knowledge, should not be promoted to episcopal honor. Therefore, considering that this deficiency can be easily detected in our presence, and unwilling to endure further detriment to the said church, we order you to assign a suitable and peremptory term for both parties, by which the said provost may appear personally and the chapter through a sufficient and appropriate procurator before us, to do and receive what the order of reason may dictate. You are to inform us of what you have done in this matter by your letters. Given at Interamn, on the 13th of March, in the tenth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX Magistro Andreae, capellano suo Bononiae commoranti, mandat ut praefigat terminum peremptorium, quo praepositus Concordiensis personaliter, capitulum vero Polense per procuratorem idoneum coram eo compareant, ut causa electionis pastoris ecclesiae Polensis, ab archidiacono et praeposito electi, dirimatur; defectus scientiae praepositi impedit promotionem eius ad episcopatum. Dat. Interamnae, III idus Martii, anno decimo.

To the dean of the Major Church and of St. Germain of Auxerre in Paris, and Master Wernacius, canon of Tervi, residing in Paris. From the letters of our venerable brother, the bishop of Tournai, we have learned that when Gerald de Bré, canon of Aentis, who holds the church of Rialhac in the diocese of Limoges, unwilling to reside there, which, according to the statutes of the council of Béziers, was thereby legally vacant and had devolved to his donation, granted the same, by the authority of the legation which he exercised in those parts, to Master Stephen Vassandi, a poor cleric, a man, as he asserts, of good testimony and honorable conduct and life, who, having studied in Paris for a long time, had ascended the masterly chair; but he, frightened by the threats of the same canon, who is noble and powerful, resigned it into the hands of the same legate. The legate, having sought out the aforementioned canon and admonished him to ascend to holy orders, as the care of the church required, since he could not be induced to do so, deprived him of the same church, and anew granted it to the aforementioned master; whom, investing him corporally with it, by the authority of the same legate, our venerable brother, the bishop of Limoges and his colleague, pronounced sentences of excommunication against the said Gerald de Bré and his accomplices for obstinately opposing him, and against those celebrating and hearing divine services in the same and its chapel without the license of the aforementioned master, and sentences of interdict against the said church and chapel. Indeed, the said canon, persisting in injury, deprived of legal support, by the frivolous pretext of an appeal which he claimed to have sent to the Apostolic See, having violently ejected the chaplains of the same master, made divine offices celebrated or rather profaned there through hired priests bound by the chain of excommunication. Furthermore, by various rescripts, one namely to the abbot and prior of Riom, and another to the provost of Brivates and his colleagues in the diocese of Clermont, and a third in which was that clause "certain others," by which he was attracted to the abbot and prior of Font Gumbaudi in the diocese of Bourges, obtained from the Apostolic See, and while the day was pending before the abbot and prior of Riom to render an interlocutory judgment on whether the same Stephen should be restored to the aforementioned church, the remaining judges summoned the same to various places not a little distant from each other. And when, with the parties appearing to hear the said interlocutory, it was amicably agreed between them, under the hope of peace, that they would cease from the prosecution of the cause for a certain time: yet within that term, Stephen himself, summoned a second time by the Brivates at the instigation of the opposing party to a certain day, although their citation did not reach him, when he did not guard against this kind of fraud, he pre-empted that day by chance, proposing by way of exception before two of them with the third colleague absent, that he should not be harassed within the space of one month by the deceit of the adversary or by direct letters to them, not making mention of the rest, as they were obtained on the same matter. But they, not admitting such an exception, after an appeal interposed by him, pronounced sentences of interdict, excommunication, and suspension against the same master, P. the priest, and others, his supporters, as it is said, and, invalidating all that had been done by the authority of the aforementioned legate, with the lawsuit not contested and he himself absent, adjudicated the church to the aforementioned canon. However, the often-mentioned cleric, coming to the Apostolic See and prolonging his stay there, humbly supplicated us to deign to provide a fitting remedy for these matters. Since, therefore, through our beloved son, Brother R., our penitentiary, we have caused him to be absolved from the sentences pronounced against him on this occasion as a precaution, he having given a sworn caution to obey our mandates on these matters for which he is said to have been interdicted and excommunicated, we mandate to your discretion by apostolic writings that you, causing all the apostolic letters and processes concerning the aforesaid to be exhibited to you, hear without delay what the parties shall have chosen to propose on either side, and, if it proceeds with the consent of the parties, terminate the cause with a canonical conclusion, making etc. Otherwise, you will sufficiently instruct it and send it back to us, appointing a competent term for the parties, by which they or their suitable procurators etc., until: they will receive. To the abbot of Tiliacum. The outcry that has long been raised against the bishop of Ventimiglia, concerning his heinous acts, has grown so strong that we can no longer ignore it with a clear conscience, nor tolerate it without danger. Among other grave matters reported by many about him, it was recently brought to our attention by our beloved sons, the archdeacon, the provost, and William de Pigna, a canon of Ventimiglia, along with certain clerics of the diocese of Ventimiglia, that this bishop, who did not enter the episcopate through the proper gate, and does not perform his duties except to harm his subjects, is so corrupted by vile acts and corrupts others by his example of perversion, that it can truly be said of him: "Man being in honor did not understand; he is compared to senseless beasts." For, having allegedly obtained the bishopric through simony, simoniacal merchants buy and sell churches and ecclesiastical benefices in his court; nothing spiritual is done there spiritually, but rather granted to the highest bidder, disregarding the fact that the Prince of the Church did not tolerate such things in Simon, nor did Elisha in Giezi, nor did Christ in the sellers of doves. Moreover, as his life is dissolute, publicly keeping a concubine, so that his subjects, corrupted by his example, more easily fall into dishonorable and shameful acts, he not only fails to correct their excesses, but rather, having received money from them, permits them to wallow in their filth. He allows marriages to be contracted in his diocese in degrees prohibited by divine law, and separates the contracted ones legally through the intervention of money. He burdens the clergy and churches of the city of Ventimiglia and the diocese with unbearable exactions and collections, from which he nourishes his illegitimate offspring and other dishonorable persons, with whom he stains himself through infamous commerce; nor does he put a limit to his greed, extorting usury from his clerics, a crime detested by both the Old and New Testaments, and dispenses with concubinarians and their sons. He also absolves those who lay hands, without consulting the Apostolic See, and slanders it publicly by lying that the Supreme Pontiff does not surpass a simple priest in granting indulgences, and that he keeps a concubine by our special indulgence; and, like salt having lost its flavor, lacking completely the condiment of wisdom, he reveals confessions made to him, against canonical sanctions. He hurls sentences of excommunication indiscriminately against church prelates and clerics subject to him, without any prior warning; and although he is bound by several sentences of excommunication, he nonetheless presumes to celebrate, indeed profane, the divine services, to the peril of his soul and the contempt of ecclesiastical discipline. Thus, he, who ought to not only preside over his subjects but also benefit them both by word and example, is a snare and downfall to many. Since these matters, if true, should not remain unexamined, wishing to go down and see if truth accompanies the outcry, we command you to diligently investigate the truth concerning these and other matters, and faithfully report to us your findings in a letter, so that, sufficiently informed by your report, we may proceed as we see fit in accordance with God; giving the bishop a suitable peremptory term to appear before us to receive what he deserves; meanwhile, forbidding him entirely any contract of mutual or alienation, declaring null and void anything done otherwise, and ensuring that those pursuing this investigation are given the necessary expenses from the goods of the church of Ventimiglia; contradictors etc. Notwithstanding the constitution of two days etc., and any apostolic indulgence you may have, that you are not obliged to judge in this matter. Given at Interamna, 10th Kalends of December, in the tenth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Papa (Gregorius IX), abbati de Tilieto mandat ut contra episcopum Vigintimiliensem, accusatum de nefandis actibus et corruptione ecclesiastica, diligenter inquirat, veritatem referat et episcopum citet ad praesentiam papalem pro meritis recepturum. Dat. Interamne, X kalendas decembris, anno decimo pontificatus.

To the Bishop of Chichester, the elected Bishop of Valence residing in England, and the Abbot of St. Augustine of Canterbury. Our beloved son, Master Robert of Gloucester, a cleric, presented before us that the church of Eineford had been lawfully conferred upon him by our authority. However, the official of Canterbury, upon the presentation of our dearest son in Christ, the illustrious King of England, after a legitimate appeal had been made to us, intruded William de Plessi, a cleric holding multiple ecclesiastical benefices with the cure of souls attached, without apostolic dispensation, into the aforementioned church, to Robert’s prejudice. Master Robert, coming before us, delivered our letters to our venerable brother, the Bishop of Worcester, and his colleagues, instructing them to call those who should be called and to hear the proposals from both sides and decide what is canonical. Meanwhile, our venerable brother, the Archbishop of Canterbury, removed William from the church, but to strengthen the opposition against Master Robert, unlawfully instituted Master William de Cemeia, who was suffering from illegitimacy and had not been dispensed by the Apostolic See, in the church, to Robert’s prejudice and grievance. When Master Robert summoned the holder before the same judges, the king, at the request of the holder, prohibited the judges from proceeding and Robert from pursuing the matter. This was reported to us by two of the judges through their letters, with one of the judges excusing himself from the entire case. It was reported that the messengers of the judges, carrying citation letters to the holder, were grievously wounded by the holder’s mandate, one of whom was a clerk. Master Robert also complained against the Archbishop, stating that the Archbishop, while defending the holder, developed a resentment against Robert because he pursued his right against him. Robert had obtained our letters to the Archbishop concerning the excessive burden of usury from certain Jews against himself and his brothers, William and Philip, who were crusaders. When Robert approached the Archbishop with these letters, the latter not only refused to accept them but also barred him from entering his court without reasonable cause. As a result, Master Robert claims he and his brothers suffered grave losses, with their books and inheritance devoured by usury due to a lack of justice. Although Master Robert, while before the Apostolic See, defended the Archbishop in the case that William de Plessi had against him regarding his removal from the church, the Archbishop, despite acknowledging the beneficial actions taken, refused to reimburse him for the expenses incurred. Therefore, since he cannot contend with the Archbishop and the intruder on equal terms, he humbly beseeched us to mercifully provide him with assistance. Since it is unseemly for us to allow Master Robert, who is in extreme poverty while pursuing our grace, to be thus confused, we command that a suitable peremptory term be set for the Archbishop and William, by which they or their suitable representatives should present themselves before us, to do and receive what justice dictates. If not all comply, then you, brother Bishop, etc. Given at Interamna, on the Nones of January, in the year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Papa Honorius III episcopo Cicestrensi, electo Valentino in Anglia commoranti, et abbati Sancti Augustini Cantuariensis mandat quatenus archiepiscopo Cantuariensi et Willelmo de Cemeia praefigant terminum peremptorium ut se nostro conspectui repraesentent, pro causa ecclesiae de Eineford, in qua magister Robertus de Glovernia gravamina sustinet. Dat. Interamne, nonis januarii, anno pontificatus nostri.

To the Archbishop of Vienne, Legate of the Apostolic See. On behalf of the consuls and the people of Montpellier, it has been presented before us that they, as Catholic men, have powerfully and tirelessly stood for the faith, defending it against heretical depravity, as their own salvation and honor. Thus, when they heard a certain rumor newly arisen that some heretics were received in their land, they were gravely saddened and very distressed. To abolish this infamy, they have offered through their messengers and letters to cleanse their land from all impurity of infidelity according to our pleasure. Therefore, confident in your prudence, we command you to personally go to the place and proceed with your usual discretion in this matter, ensuring that the deadly plague does not go unpunished and the innocent are not held accountable; for the weeds must be eradicated, and the wheat should not be plucked out. Moreover, as we should be found ready to show grace to those who truly repent, we desire and command that to those who, having abandoned the heretical depravity, voluntarily, before any inquisition about them has been made, have returned or shall return to the unity of the Church, you grant the benefit of absolution from the sentence of excommunication which is solemnly pronounced by the Roman Pontiff against heretics three times a year, after they have publicly abjured the heresy and given suitable assurance that they will not relapse into the contagion of heretics, by apostolic authority following the form of the Church, and moreover, that you make the ecclesiastical sacraments be administered to them as to the faithful; and thus let it be done that they, rejoicing to have found what belongs to the mother, be rendered, by the grace of the Lord, steadfast in faith and effective in good works. Given at Interamna, on the 4th day before the calends of March, in the tenth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX archiepiscopo Viennensi, Apostolicae Sedis legato mandat ut ad Montem Pesulanum accedat et hereticos in ea receptatos aboleat, praebens vere poenitentibus et ad Ecclesiam redeuntibus, post abjurationem, absolutionem et sacramenta ecclesiastica. Datum Interamnae, IV kalendas martii, anno decimo.

**Translation to English:**

To the podestà, councilors, and people of Vercelli. Strangers to the Christian faith, indeed, our venerable brother, the Bishop of Vercelli, has brought to our attention that, despite the letters and command we directed to you to abolish the statutes issued against his church, which afflict it in many ways by imposing taxes and burdens on his clergy and people, and to desist from such grievances while preserving their freedom inviolably, with the Archbishop of Milan appointed as executor by the Apostolic See for these matters: you, however, closed your ears like a deaf asp, and the same archbishop placed your city under interdict; and when this did not have any effect on you, he personally came to the city, accompanied by our venerable brothers, the Cardinal of Palestrina, then a legate of the Apostolic See, and the bishops of Novara, Ivrea, and Turin, vehemently urging and admonishing you, firmly instructing you to prefer obedience over ruin, and humbly comply with our wishes in this matter. But you, as if you had made a pact with death, scorned to do this, with the podestà responding arrogantly that you would neither present the book of statutes as requested nor remove the statutes from your records, furthermore threatening those clergy and people with destruction. Therefore, we solemnly admonish, beseech, and exhort your entire community through our apostolic writings, commanding that you fulfill the aforementioned requests and make amends for the harm and injuries inflicted; otherwise, since you, wounding the bowels of your mother church of Vercelli with the sword, compel us to the necessity of not sparing you, we give our letters to our venerable brother, the Bishop of Novara, instructing him to ensure that you, as excommunicated, are strictly avoided by everyone, prohibiting any trade with you, forbidding anyone to assume the role of podestà or rector among you, and prohibiting anyone from attending the fairs of Vercelli or that students remain in your city further; restraining the disobedient and rebellious through ecclesiastical censure, if necessary, postponing any appeal. Given at Interamna, on the Nones of March.

**Regesto in Latin:**

**Gregorius IX** potestati, consiliariis et populo Vercellensibus mandat ut statuta contra ecclesiam Vercellensem edita abolant, desistentes a gravaminibus et libertatem clericorum et hominum conservando; alioquin episcopo Novariensi mandat ut eos tanquam excommunicatos evitari faciat et commercium interdicat. **Dat. Interamne, nonis martii, anno pontificatus tertio.**

Translation to English:

To all archbishops and bishops established throughout the kingdom of France. He who fashioned the hearts of all men knows fully how urgent the matter of the Holy Land presses upon us, as we aspire with all our desires and affections towards its liberation. Hence, not without bitterness of heart, we have heard from our dearest son in Christ, the illustrious King of France, through his letters and envoy, that certain signed with the cross residing in the kingdom of France, who ought to have the fear of the Lord and divine love ever before the eyes of their minds, so as to commit nothing by which they might offend the divine majesty, have, fascinated by diabolical cunning, borne the assumed sign of the life-giving cross as if under compulsion, and having given a writ of divorce to virtues, thus have contracted with vices, trusting in the privilege granted to those signed with the cross of impunity, whereby the utility of the matter is greatly diminished, not without the scandal of many. We command your community that each of you in your dioceses should thus endeavor to ensure that crimes do not remain unpunished, and that those signed with the cross are not deprived of the privilege granted to them, unless the wickedness of those signed with the cross is such that this privilege ought not to support them. Given at Terni, 10th February, in the tenth year [of our pontificate].

Regesto in Latin:

Gregorius Papa IX universis archiepiscopis et episcopis per regnum Franciae mandat ut in suis diocesibus provideant ne crimina crucesignatorum impunita maneant, nec privilegio priventur, nisi eorum nequitia talem privationem exigat. Datum Interamnae, IIII idus februarii, anno decimo.

Translation to English:

To the masters S. Pagani, Parisian, Hugon, Pisan, and P. called Caligarius, Morinensian, residing in Paris, canons. Know that it has come to our hearing, by our beloved son master Guillelmus, canon of Bayeux, that Oddo de Villa Terrici, former dean of Bayeux, on the day he was elected dean, swore in the chapter of Bayeux that without delay, as soon as he could, he would have himself ordained as a priest, as the administration of the deanery, which entails the care of souls, and also the custom of the church required. However, neglecting to fulfill this, disregarding the sanctity of his oath, it is said that the church of Bayeux suffered not a little detriment both spiritually and temporally. Finally, after seven years elapsed, shamelessly casting off clerical habit and tonsure, to the detriment of his soul and the scandal of many, he became a secular knight, and in the presence of our venerable brother, the archbishop of Sens, and many others, falsely swearing that he did not have holy orders, he unlawfully married the daughter of the knight Gaufridus of Bulliaco. Later, realizing that some sought to accuse this so-called marriage or rather cohabitation, and wishing to return to the deanery which he had by that fact renounced, he made a fraudulent appeal to us, preventing the Bayeux canons, his supporters, from proceeding to elect a dean in the said church. Therefore, we were humbly entreated to provide for this church with fatherly care. Since these matters are said to be notorious in those parts, so that they cannot be concealed, we command, with the consent of both parties, that if it is evident to you that this is the case, you order the said chapter to provide for themselves within three months by canonical election, as pertains to them, for a dean. Otherwise, instruct our venerable brother, the bishop of Bayeux, to provide for the church by our authority with a suitable person as dean. What if not all agree, etc. Notwithstanding the constitution enacted in the general council about two diets, provided that one party does not drag the other beyond the third or fourth part outside their diocese for judgment. Given at Interamna, on the 26th of February, in the tenth year.

To the subdean and archdeacon of Pissiacenti and Chartres. A petition presented to us by the treasurer, dean, and chapter of the church of Saint Hilary of Poitiers stated that a dispute had arisen between them, on one side, and the noblewoman Haynord, called the lady of Belle Lieu, who is said to hold residences in the dioceses of Bourges and Auxerre, on the other side, concerning the grave damages and injuries she inflicted upon them and their people to their prejudice, as well as certain incomes and other matters. After various commissions on this matter were obtained from the Apostolic See to different judges, we, wishing to safeguard the indemnities of the parties, directed our writings to our venerable brother, the Archbishop of Tours, and his colleagues, to resolve the case by fair judgment or agreement if the parties were willing. Otherwise, they were to refer the case back to us sufficiently instructed, setting a peremptory and suitable term by which they should present themselves to our presence by themselves or by suitable procurators. This process was impeded by an objection from the other party. However, since, as they claim, due to the evasions of the aforementioned noblewoman, the case has been delayed for more than twenty years without reaching the point of contesting the suit, and due to these delays and other grievances by which she oppresses them, compelling them, out of weariness, to desist from pursuing their rights, the aforementioned church has been considerably depleted in its resources. They supplicated that paternal providence comes to their aid in this matter. Therefore, wishing to avert troubles, as we desire peace for all, we command that a peremptory and suitable term be set for the aforementioned noblewoman by which she should appear before our presence by herself or by a suitable procurator to prosecute the issued appeal and proceed even on the principal matter. Moreover, you must prudently receive and diligently examine elderly and infirm witnesses and other suitable ones, whose death or prolonged absence is feared, whom the treasurer, dean, and chapter may produce before you on this matter, so that the opportunity of proof is not taken away by chance events. You should have their statements compiled into public documents. If they perhaps withdraw out of favor, hatred, or fear, you must compel them through ecclesiastical censure, with no appeal allowed, to testify to the truth, notifying the aforementioned noblewoman to be present, if she wishes, at the witness reception, and to have a public instrument drawn up regarding the notification thus made. Notwithstanding the constitution about two diets, etc., provided that beyond the third or fourth, the other party, etc. Given at the Lateran, 12th day before the Ides of January, in the eleventh year.

Cum causa viginti annis protrahatur, mandat ut nobilis terminum peremptorium habeat quo coram se vel procuratore in causa se sistat. To the Archbishop of Thebes, the Bishop of Negroponte, and the Archdeacon of Thebes. Our beloved son, Cortatius, the elected of Chyron, appeared in our presence and with tearful complaint informed us that, after the Chyron church was left without a pastor and the appointment was devolved to our venerable brother, the Archbishop of Crete, the metropolitan of the place, according to the statutes of the general council, the said archbishop, considering the state of the church and wishing to provide it with a suitable person, appointed him, then the cantor of the church, educated in both Latin and Greek letters and devoted to the Apostolic See, as pastor of the church. Subsequently, while he was working to reach our presence, he was captured by some pirates. Despite this, the Archdeacon of Crete, without mentioning the foregoing or that the archbishop had nullified an election made by some intruders after an appeal was made to us, falsely suggested that he had been canonically elected by the chapter of the aforementioned church and that the archbishop had unjustly refused to confirm his election. In the name of the chapter of the church, he obtained our letters directed to the archbishop to confirm his election if it was found to have been celebrated canonically with a suitable person. The Bishop of Gerapetra was also instructed by other letters from us that if the archbishop neglected our mandate, he should execute it. The same archdeacon, although he did not present our letters to the archbishop, claimed that the election made of him had been confirmed by apostolic authority and forcibly occupied the episcopate of Chyron, intruding some as canons and others into the dignities of the mentioned church. Although the archbishop decreed that what had been presumed concerning these intruders was null and void, condemning them to restore the fruits they had received and excommunicating them if they interfered with the administration of the church, yet they nevertheless detain the episcopate mentioned, wastefully indulging in its goods. Since the elected has obtained our letters to the chancellor and masters Odo and Frederick, canons of Constantinople, in common form concerning these and other articles, with the chancellor committing his duties to his co-judges or one of them, one of whom has died and the other has not processed the matter, but referred it back to our judgment entirely unexamined. Therefore, the elected humbly begged us to provide for him and the church of Chyron with fatherly care concerning this and also because the aforementioned intruders have laid violent hands upon him, disregarding the fear of God, for which the archbishop publicly declared them excommunicated. Therefore, we command that if it is certain to you about the violent laying on of hands, you declare those sacrilegious ones, etc., as far as absolving them. As for the other matters, after summoning those who are to be called and hearing the proposals from both sides, you send the case back to us sufficiently instructed, setting a suitable peremptory term for the parties to present themselves before us to receive a just sentence, with the Lord's aid. If any impediment arises preventing you from proceeding with the instruction of the case, nevertheless set a suitable peremptory term for the parties, at which they are to appear personally or through sufficient and suitable procurators before us to do and receive what the order of law dictates. And lest the abundance of proofs be withdrawn from the elected by chance occurrences over time, ensure that you receive and carefully examine old and infirm witnesses, whose death or long absence is feared, on the articles we send you enclosed under our seal, first notifying the other party so that, if they wish, they may be present at the reception of testimonies, and have a public instrument made about the notification thus done. Furthermore, provide that the necessary expenses for the prosecution of the matter be supplied to the elected from the goods of the same church while the matter is pending, ensuring that the episcopate does not suffer the waste of dilapidation under the uncertainty of the lawsuit's outcome; those opposing, etc. Given at Interamna, on the 11th day before the Ides of February, in the tenth year.

Dat. Interamnae, III idus februarii, anno decimo.
