Gregorius IX magistris scolarum Januensi et archipresbytero de Aguscio, Januensis diocesis, mandat quatenus, si Ansaldus presbiter falsasse sigillum et litteras confiterit, ipsum pena canonica, sublato appellationis obstaculo, castigent et detineri faciant, donec sufficientem cautelam prestiterit, ne ecclesiam aut beneficiarios molestet. Dat. Laterani, XV kalendas aprilis, pontificatus nostri anno quarto.

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop of Strigonia, legate of the Apostolic See in Cumania. With the beloved son. Given at Rieti, on the 11th day before the calends of August, in the sixth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Papa Gregorius IX archiepiscopo Strigoniensi, in Cumania Apostolicae Sedis legato, mandat quatenus cum dilecto filio agere. Datum Reate, XI kalendas augusti, anno sexto.

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop, the Abbot of Saint Catherine, and the Archdeacon of Calais, Rouen. It has come to our attention, as communicated by Egidia, the lady of Saint Andrew and widow, that when she brought a lawsuit against R. de Cortiniaco, a knight of the diocese of Sens, concerning certain revenues and other matters pertaining to her dowry, before the dean of Rouen and his co-judges, by the authority of our beloved son R., the elected of Porto and then legate of the Apostolic See, the said knight eventually raised an objection that the case concerning immovable properties related to the dowry should be heard in the secular court according to the custom of the land. Since the judges, as they were obliged, did not admit such an exception, he appealed to our hearing. Considering his appeal frivolous, they pronounced excommunication upon him for contumacy, and placed his land under interdict. When the aforementioned knight, fabricating another cause of grievance, obtained letters from us directed to the dean of Chartres and his colleagues, they, setting aside the appeal and not observing the form of the apostolic mandate, decreed by interlocutory that the first grievance was sufficient and that the said knight had legitimately appealed from it, revoking the process of the said judges as presumed after a legitimate appeal. Wherefore the said widow issued an appeal to us, which she could not pursue due to long illness and other legitimate impediments, two years having already elapsed. She implored an apostolic remedy for this. Therefore we command that if this is so, having revoked anything found attempted concerning this appeal, you shall legitimately inquire into the aforementioned processes, and ensure that what is canonical is done, etc. Witnesses, etc. If not all, etc. Given at Rieti, the 8th Ides of March, in the fifth year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX archiepiscopo, abbati Sanctae Catherinae et archidiacono de Caleto Rothomagensibus mandat ut, causam Egidiae dominae de Sancto Andrea viduae contra R. de Cortiniaco militem de redditibus et rebus ad dotalicium spectantibus inspectam, si quid adversus appellationem repertum sit, revocent et processus legitime cognoscant, sublato impedimento appellationis frivolam reputatae. Dat. Reate, VIII idus martii, anno quinto.

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop of Bordeaux. Until now, the patience of the Apostolic See has been excessively tested by your cunning calumnies and evasive delays regarding the case between you and our venerable brother, the Archbishop of Bourges, concerning the primacy that the Archbishop of Bourges claims to possess over you and the church and province of Bordeaux. However, when you saw yourself ensnared in your own cunning and almost rebelliously persevering, which we can no longer endure with patience, after your various evasions and following the protest made by your procurator on the day we appointed for proposing all delays, that only three dilatory exceptions could be proposed and proven at another term to be set for you, namely excommunication, spoliation, and that the Archbishop of Bourges could not act in this case without the consent of his suffragans, we remember firmly ordering you by our letters to present yourself, either in person or through a suitable representative, before us on the feast of the Nativity of the Lord just past, which we set as your peremptory term, prepared for the above, as well as for the contestation of the suit and to fully respond, after deliberation with those you deem expedient, to all that pertains to the resolution of the case. We also directed our letters to our beloved sons, the Abbot of Aque Vive in the diocese of Tours, and the Archdeacon of Tours, to cite you to the same peremptory term, and if you could not be found, to ensure that the edict of citation be publicly offered at your church, with them informing us of their actions. Indeed, with the Archdeacon entrusting his role to our beloved son John, the cellarer of Aque Vive, the aforementioned Abbot and Cellarer, obedient to apostolic mandates, personally traveled to the city of Bordeaux and, finding you there, cited you peremptorily with a live voice according to the form given to them, offering you the letters of citation addressed to the Abbot and Archdeacon, with the said Cellarer offering the letters entrusted to him by the Archdeacon. However, upon hearing mention of the citation and seeing our other letters in their hands, you immediately turned your face away from them, and consequently, some of those who were with you then sacrilegiously struck the said Abbot with fists and sticks in your presence, and violently took from his hands the letters we had sent to the Abbot and Archdeacon as he offered them to you, leaving the bull, the string, and a piece of parchment in his hands; and while these things were happening, the Cellarer and Master P. de Laverge, who had come with them, repeatedly offered you the letters of citation directed to you, but you refused to receive them, as the oft-mentioned Abbot and Cellarer have informed us in their letters. Nevertheless, although perhaps no further citation should be sent to you, but rather a penalty imposed, to shame the wickedness of such malice, since we do not wish, nor indeed should we, to prolong the case further in your favor, we firmly command your fraternity by the authority of these presents that, with every excuse or exception entirely set aside, you personally present yourself before us by the octave of the upcoming feast of Saint Andrew the Apostle, which we set as your peremptory term beyond which you should not believe you will be awaited if you do not appear then, prepared and instructed for the above and other matters pertaining to the resolution of the case, responding both to possessory and, if an action is brought against you, also to the petitionary matters. Given at Rieti, on the thirteenth calends of September, in the fifth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto:**

Pope Honorius III orders the Archbishop of Bordeaux to appear before him by the octave of the feast of Saint Andrew the Apostle for the case concerning the primacy claimed by the Archbishop of Bourges, dismissing all excuses and exceptions, underlining previous attempts at citation and the violent refusal thereof. Issued in Rieti, on the thirteenth calends of September, in the fifth year of his pontificate.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Burgos, and the Deans of Burgos and Calahorra. We are amazed if what has recently reached our ears about our dearest son in Christ, the illustrious King of Castile, is true. For we have heard that the same king, by trampling upon the rights and liberties of the Church of Calahorra in many ways, promulgated certain statutes to the detriment of that church under the penalty of losing his favor and property, by a new command of his own that no one in the diocese of Calahorra should dare to donate or sell any possessions to the cathedral church, or to monasteries, or other pious places of the same diocese. Not content with this, he ordered that possessions sold or donated without the authority of his letters or those of his grandfather from the time when his grandfather held court at Nájera should be confiscated; he also takes away the possessions of the same church and religious places, and allows undue exactions to be imposed upon them. Moreover, in contempt of the statute on Jews issued at the general council, he prohibited, according to his own will, that the Jews should wear distinguishing badges, or that tithes should be imposed on inheritances which have come to them from Christians, even though our venerable brother, the Bishop of Sabina, then legate of the Apostolic See, ordered these statutes to be observed; because of this, many parish churches have been almost completely reduced to nothing, as the possessions from which tithes used to be paid to them have been turned over to Jews through usurious practices. It is also said that he commanded that all the ecclesiastical goods of deceased clerics should devolve to their sons or heirs, by which occasion, reducing the liberty of the Church of Calahorra to the disgrace of servitude, he has stripped it of certain possessions of one of its canons, who died intestate, although he had possessed them peacefully for some time. Since, however, we love him with abundant charity, we have decided to exhort and admonish the royal majesty more earnestly, beseeching him by the only begotten Son of God, Jesus Christ, and likewise advising him in good faith, that as a Christian king and Catholic prince, he should consider that the Lord did not grant him the power of the sword for him to wield it against the churches, which he is rather obligated to defend from others, and to refrain from the aforementioned enormities, which, although not spoken of, the well-known grievances of the church proclaim. For his honor and the salvation of his soul, he should desist entirely and restore with integrity what has been taken, and not delay to revoke such statutes, commands, and prohibitions, so that he may be able to appease God, whom we do not doubt he has offended in these matters, and so that the Roman Church, which seems to be gravely shaken in the Church of Calahorra as in one of its members, may not be compelled to pursue these matters otherwise. Therefore, we command your discretion through apostolic writings to diligently admonish and induce the same king on our behalf to do this, reporting back to us without delay on what you have found. If not all of you can act together, then you, Bishop, along with one of the others, should act. Given at the Lateran, on the fourth day before the nones of April, in the fifth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX episcopo Burgensi et decanis Burgensi et Calagurritano mandat ut regem Castellae admoneant et inducant ad revocandas statuta et prohibitiones quae jura et libertates ecclesiae Calagurritanae laedunt, et restitutionem rerum ablatarum efficiendam. Dat. Laterani, II nonas aprilis, pontificatus nostri anno quinto.

**Translation to English:**

To the archdeacon of Norwich. It has come to our attention, as reported by our beloved son Master Martin de Summa, our subdeacon and rector of the church of Domerham, that after several commissions, he brought the abbot and convent of Glastonbury and a certain cleric, of the dioceses of Bath and Salisbury, to trial concerning the chapel of Merton, which pertains to the said church, before the dean of Exeter and his co-judges by apostolic authority. The judges, deciding both on the possessory and the proprietary matters brought before them, pronounced a definitive sentence in his favor, as justice required. However, the opposing party frivolously appealed, and after he had regained possession of the aforementioned chapel, from which he had been unlawfully stripped, and had held it peacefully and without dispute for some time after the appeal, the said party sent a messenger to obtain letters concerning their appeal to the Apostolic See and meanwhile forcibly ejected him from the mentioned chapel. Later, when he proposed before the chancellor of Wells and his colleagues, to whom letters had been obtained concerning the aforesaid appeal, that since the appeal was pending, the opposing party had stripped him, he was not obliged to respond unless restitution was first made. Because these judges did not admit such an exception, he appealed to our hearing; thus he humbly requested that, since the case has been long protracted between him and his predecessors on one side, and the aforementioned abbot and convent on the other, and he fears it may be further delayed due to the malice of the opposing party, we might mercifully intervene on this matter. Therefore, we command your discretion by apostolic writings that, if this is so, after restituting him as is just and annulling whatever may have been rashly attempted after the said appeal, you shall hear the case and, if it proceeds with the consent of the parties, bring it to a rightful conclusion, or remit it sufficiently instructed to our presence, setting a competent term for the parties to present themselves before our sight either personally or through an adequate procurator, to receive a just sentence, God willing; otherwise, you shall remit them to the examination of the said chancellor and his colleagues. Appellant etc. Witnesses etc. Notwithstanding the constitution made in the general council about the two days, provided that by this the other party is not dragged beyond the third or fourth day. Given at Lateran, the sixth day before the kalends of June, in the fifth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Papa Honorius III archidiacono Norwicensi mandat ut, restituto Martino de Summa in possessionem capellae de Merton, causam inter eum et abbatem Glastoniensem audiat aut sufficienter instructam ad sedem Apostolicam remittat, datis partibus terminis competentibus. Dat. Laterani, VI kalendas junii, anno quinto.

Translation to English:

To the abbot and the prior of Terre Majoris, of the diocese of Ciudad. On behalf of the beloved. Given at Anagni, on the 7th day before the Ides of September, in the sixth year of our pontificate.

Regesto in Latin:

Papa (likely Honorius III or Gregorius IX) abbati et priori Terre Majoris, Civitatensis diocesis, ut causam dilecti prosequantur, mandat. Datum Anagnie, VII idus septembris, anno pontificatus nostri sexto.

**Translation to English:**

To the abbots of Bochon and Tichon, and the archdeacon of Roba, of the dioceses of Veszprém and Győr. During the time of blessed memory. Given at Rieti, on the tenth day before the calends of August, in the sixth year. It is written on this matter in the manner of confirmation to the Bishop of Zagreb and the chapter. In the same manner to the abbot and convent of the Monastery of Saint Martin in Pannonia.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Papa [nomen pontificis] abbatibus de Bochon et Tichon, et archidiacono de Roba, Vesprimiensis et Jauriensis diocesium, mandat ad confirmandum scriptum super hoc, sicut episcopo Zagrabiensi et capitulo, et abbati ac conventui monasterii Sancti Martini de Pannonia. Dat. Reate, X kalendas augusti, anno sexto.

**Translation to English:**

To the Chapter of Messina. Whereas a case that had long been litigated between the late archbishop of Messina of good memory, on one side, and the abbot and convent of the monastery of St. Savior of Lingua Messanensis, on the other, concerning subjection, obedience, and reverence, was resolved by the provision of the Apostolic See; and because the same convent, ungrateful as they were, disregarded the grace extended to them in such provision and presumptuously acted against the same provision, our venerable brother, the archbishop of Regio and his colleagues, by the authority of our predecessor, Pope Honorius, of happy memory, pronounced a sentence of excommunication against them. This sentence was later commanded to be observed inviolably until due satisfaction by the archbishop of Cosenza and his co-judges by apostolic authority. Despite this, the abbot mentioned died bound by the excommunication, and the convent, having obtained absolution from our venerable brother, the archbishop of Capua, then Bishop of Pactum, continued with their pre-conceived malice. They elected Mathary, one of their monks and brethren, as abbot of the monastery and refused to present the election for examination and confirmation to the aforementioned archbishop of Messina, thereby violating the provision and oath taken. Consequently, our venerable brothers, the bishops of Milazzo and Tropea, publicly pronounced them excommunicated and perjured, reducing them to the original sentence of excommunication by apostolic authority. Although the process of these bishops was approved by the beloved son, the abbot of Nucaria, and his colleagues by apostolic mandate, the convent continued for almost a year in obstinate excommunication, treating the ecclesiastical keys with disdain. Thus, our predecessor instructed our venerable brother, the bishop of Cefalù, and his colleagues to visit the monastery personally and remove the said elected abbot and order the archbishop of Messina to provide a new abbot for the monastery. However, due to the maliciousness of the time, they could not execute the apostolic mandate. Therefore, at the petition of the same convent, we delegated our venerable brother, the bishop of Marturano and the beloved son, the abbot of St. Stephen of Bosco, by our letters to go to the place personally, receive a sworn guarantee from the convent to obey our mandates and grant them the benefit of absolution so that you and the convent were to present yourselves before us within two months after obtaining absolution through suitable procurators with a special mandate, to humbly accept our mandate regarding the aforementioned matters. Thus, with the beloved sons, Master B., canon of Messina, and Virgil, canon of Traina, appearing on your behalf before us, and P. and G., procurators of the said convent, we appointed our beloved son, Cardinal E., deacon of the Saints Cosmas and Damian, as auditor. Before him, your procurators requested the execution of the provision, the punishment of the elected and the convent for celebrating divine offices while perjured and excommunicated, and the removal of the elected abbot who administered for six years without confirmation, to the grave detriment of the Messina church, according to the mandate of our predecessor. In contrast, the convent's procurators denied that they or the convent celebrated divine offices while excommunicated, arguing that the provision was excessively harsh in several chapters and could not be observed as it derogated from their privileges. They requested that its severity be tempered by the Apostolic See. After the cardinal had prudently and faithfully reported these matters and others to us and our brothers, we decreed from the counsel of our brothers that the named provision be firmly observed and the elected abbot completely removed from the governance of the monastery, strictly commanding the procurators, in the name of their convent, under the obligation of their oath, to ensure the provision is observed inviolably. Let no one therefore etc., infringe on our decree. If anyone, however, etc. Given at the Lateran, on the seventh of the Kalends of June, in the fifth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Papa Gregorius IX capitulo Messanensi mandat ut provisionem Sedis Apostolicae super subjectione et obedientia monasterii Sancti Salvatoris de Lingua Messanensis inviolabiliter observent, et electum archimandritam amoveant propter administrationem non confirmatam; dat. Laterani, VII kalendas junii, anno quinto pontificatus.

**Translation to English:**

To the dean of Arras. We have received the complaint of our beloved sons, the dean and chapter of Saint Fursey and the clergy of Péronne, stating that when they purchase any house in the town of Péronne from laypeople, the mayor, aldermen, and sworn officials of the same town, in the diocese of Noyon, act injuriously and grievously towards them as much as they can, troubling the laypeople on account of this in many ways, placing them under their ban and burdening them with undue exactions. To excuse themselves, they beg frivolous excuses so as not to seem to harass the laypeople for this cause. Thus, it happens that, due to fear of penalty, no one is found there who dares to sell any house to them for any price, to the considerable detriment of the aforementioned, who, in this regard, are in a worse condition than the laypeople. Therefore, they have humbly implored us to kindly provide for them in this matter with paternal care. Not wishing to sustain the undue grievance against the said dean, chapter, and clergy, we strictly command you through apostolic writings to compel the aforementioned mayor and aldermen, with previous admonition, to cease entirely from their undue harassment, by means of ecclesiastical censure, postponing any appeal, after reason has been established. Given at Anagni, on the 17th day before the Kalends of October, in the year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Papa (Gregorius IX) decano Atrebatensi mandat quatenus majorem et scabinos ville Peronensis, dioecesis Noviomensis, monitione premissa, per censuram ecclesiasticam compellat ab indebita molestatione decani et capituli Sancti Fursei ac clericorum Peronensium desistentes. Datum Anagnie, XVII kalendas octobris, pontificatus nostri anno quinto.

**Translation to English:**

To the bishop of Kimis. The beloved son Radulfus. Given at Rieti, on the third day before the Kalends of August, in the sixth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Papa episcopo Kimisensi mandat de dilecto filio Radulfo. Datum Reate, III kalendas augusti, anno sexto.

**Translation to English:**

To the venerable brother, the Archbishop of Tyre, and his successors canonically to be established, in perpetuity. From the time the Church of Tyre... Following the example of our predecessors of blessed memory, Innocent, Anastasius, Adrian, Clement, and Celestine, Roman Pontiffs, supporting the same church with apostolic protection, we confirm by the authority of the Apostolic See the use of the pallium, which signifies the fullness of the pontifical office, and both for you and your successors, the right to carry the cross before you throughout the entire metropolis of Tyre, establishing that all bishoprics, whatever possessions, whatever goods the Church of Tyre presently possesses justly and canonically, and all rights pertaining to the same church, remain firm and inviolate for you and your successors. We also decree that all places held by the Saracens, which are known to have been under the jurisdiction of Tyre, once liberated from their control with the help of divine grace, shall not be occupied by anyone else but shall remain perpetually unshaken under the disposition and ordering of the Church of Tyre by our authority. Furthermore, we protect with the authority of this present writing the parish rights, good customs, both in the matter of funeral rites and tithes of the Tyrian diocese, and also in baptisms and the blessing of brides, and the purifications of women, which by ancient custom are owed solely to the mother church, and whatever that venerable place can gain by reasonable means, with God's favor. We also decree that all priests who are now or may in the future be within the bounds of the Tyrian parish, although the churches where they are appointed may belong to another by right of foundation, shall answer to you in spiritual matters and render due obedience, saving our indulgences. Nor may anyone grant any church from your parish without your consent, nor presumptuously dare to usurp what belongs to another. We decree, therefore, etc., up to disturb. If anyone, therefore, etc. To all, however, etc. Amen. Given at Rieti, by the hand of Master Martin, Archdeacon of Siena, Vice-Chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the fourteenth day before the calends of March, in the fifth indiction, in the year of the Lord's Incarnation 1232, in the fifth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Gregory IX.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX venerabili fratri archiepiscopo Tyrensi eiusque successoribus canonice substituendis concedit usum pallei et crucem deferendi, possessiones et iura ecclesiae Tyrensis confirmat, decrevit ut loca a Sarracenis detenta, post liberationem, sub dispositione Tyrensis ecclesiae maneant, et statuit ut presbyteri intra terminos parrochiae Tyrensis de spiritualibus respondeant. Dat. Reate, XIV kalendas martii, pontificatus anno quinto.

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop of Besançon. The letters presented to us by you and our venerable brothers, the Archbishops of Vienne and Tarentaise, as well as the Bishops of Grenoble and Maurienne, and also the beloved sons, the prior and chapter of the church of Belley, along with several abbots of the Cistercian order, contained that recently, the same church being deprived of the solace of a shepherd, the said prior and chapter meeting together to discuss the appointment of a future bishop, invoked the grace of the Holy Spirit, and unanimously and concordantly, with only one exception who neither explicitly consented nor contradicted, conferred their votes upon the beloved son B., son of the nobleman, the Count of Savoy, who is still in minor orders, a man, as they assert, prudent and discreet, notable for the honesty of his morals, and competently educated in the knowledge of letters, to be humbly requested from us as their pastor, as they hope through him to liberate the church from the many pressures it has suffered up to now and continuously suffers from the malice of neighboring tyrants. Therefore, they humbly requested us to mercifully dispense him regarding the defect of age, as he has not yet reached his twenty-sixth year, and to admit their request, and to grant him to them as their pastor from the kindness of the Apostolic See. Therefore, having full confidence in your discretion, we command that you examine him concerning his life, knowledge, and morals, and diligently inquire about his age, and, having considered the necessity and utility of the aforementioned church and taking all circumstances into account, if it is established that he is of competent learning and honorable conduct, and has reached his twenty-sixth year, notwithstanding the defect of age, you shall commit the care of the named church to him, both spiritual and temporal, ensuring that due obedience and reverence be exhibited to him by the aforementioned chapter, clergy, and the people of the city and diocese of Belley. As for those who contradict, etc. You shall also subsequently have him promoted to the order of subdiaconate in the forthcoming Ember Days. Otherwise, you shall diligently admonish and induce the prior and the aforementioned chapter to provide for themselves, within a set time that you shall determine, a suitable person through canonical election as bishop and pastor. Given at Spoleto, the second day before the Nones of July, in the sixth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Papa Honorius III archiepiscopo Bisuntino mandat ut B., filium comitis Sabaudie, ad curam ecclesiae Bellicensis in spiritualibus et temporalibus, ob etatis defectum dispensando, committat, si idoneus repertus fuerit, et ad subdiaconatus ordinem in Quatuor Temporibus promoveat, vel alioquin priorem et capitulum inducat ad electionem canonicam faciendam. Dat. Spoleti, II nonas julii, anno sexto.

**Translation to English:**

To the Chapter of Massa. With the church of Massa vacant of a pastor, the canons of the same church elected two of their own, namely the archpriest and M., along with some nobles called vicedomini, who claimed to have a longstanding right in the election of the bishop of Massa. They reached an agreement that these two, or one of them, with the consent of the three remaining or two, would have the power to elect someone as bishop of Massa. The mentioned archpriest delegated his authority to the three remaining, who elected our beloved son G., a canon of Pisa, as bishop of Massa. They presented this election to our venerable brother, the Archbishop of Pisa, who, when G.'s procurator was insistently seeking the confirmation of G.'s election, and the procurators of the Massa chapter were asking for the confirmation of another election they claimed to have subsequently made, the procurators, having brought forth certain objections and appeals to us, withdrew from the audience of the mentioned archbishop. The archbishop, considering their objections and appeals frivolous, confirmed the election of the aforementioned G. with metropolitan authority. Once the parties were present before the Apostolic See, and our beloved son R., the cardinal deacon of Santa Maria in Cosmedin, was appointed their auditor, and when it was fully established before him by confessions of the parties and legitimate documents concerning the above matters, and he faithfully reported these to us, we, noting that the prescribed election was presumed against the general and approved custom of the Church and the holy canons, which is proven to be multiply flawed, both from the persons of the electors as well as from such an informal form, since laymen cannot create a bishop or compromise in spiritual matters, as no authority to dispose of ecclesiastical matters, which is even less, is attributed to them, who are meant to obey in such matters, not to command, we utterly annul the aforementioned election and everything that has followed from it, with the counsel of our brothers. To prevent the spread of such a detestable example, we perpetually prohibit with an edict that henceforth no election of a bishop in the aforementioned church shall be presumed by laymen with the canons. If it is presumed, it shall hold no validity. Notwithstanding any contrary custom, which should rather be called corruption. Let no one, therefore, violate our prohibition. If anyone does, etc. Given at Rieti, on the sixth day before the nones of August, in the fifth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius Papa IX Capitulum Massanum mandat electionem episcopi Massani ab archipresbytero et nobilibus laicis factam, ut contra Ecclesiae consuetudinem et canones, irritam esse, edicto prohibens ne in posterum talis electio fiat. Dat. Reate, II nonas augusti, pontificatus nostri anno quinto.

**Translation to English:**

To the noble man Manuel Cominiano. We have kindly received the letters which your nobility sent to us via our beloved son, the noble man Theodorus, and we have diligently understood both the series of those letters and what the same noble and beloved son L., prior of the church of Saint Mary of Porto Anconitane, took care to explain to us on your behalf. We give worthy thanks to the giver of all graces because, as we have clearly seen contained in those same letters, by His healthy inspiration, you have chosen to abandon the footsteps of your former brother T., and humbly submit yourself to Him who exalts the humble to salvation. Having conceived the spirit of salvation, you humbly acknowledge the holy Roman Church as your mother, and you, devotedly, according to our benevolent will, offer up whatever you are and whatever you have. You petition us, through the same noble, that since you wish to retain the land you hold through the same Church, we would deign to receive you under our and the Apostolic See's protection. Indeed, bearing paternal care for you, we love you sincerely in the Lord as a special son of the Apostolic See, and as much as we can with the Lord, we freely wish to assent to your increase and those things which you justly seek from us, as much as we can with God. However, because full trust could not be given to us regarding what is more expedient for this, and therefore we cannot give you a certain answer, we send envoys and letters to our dearest son in Christ, the illustrious Emperor J., and our venerable brother, the patriarch of Constantinople. We instruct them to diligently inquire about the aforementioned matters and all their circumstances, and faithfully inform us by their letters about what they find concerning these things, so that we may proceed accordingly, as we see better expedient according to God. Once their response is received, with God's favor, we will proceed in the aforesaid business, omitting nothing of the contingencies, which will satisfy God to the best of our ability and man, and your devotion will not undeservedly accept it. Meanwhile, persist in our and the Roman Church's devotion, since you can firmly believe and hope that the sincerity of your devotion will respond favorably to you. Given at Rieti, on the Kalends of April, in the sixth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Papa Honorius III, nobili viro Manueli Cominiano scribit: litteras suas per Theodorum transmissas accepit, et gratias agit quod, Deo inspirante, fraterna vestigia deserens, se Ecclesie Romane humiliter subicit et protectionem petit. Propter hoc, sollicitudinem paternitatem gerens, eum sub protectione sedis Apostolice recipere velle significat, sed responsionem certam differt usque ad inquisitionem a J. imperatore et patriarcha Constantinopolitano institutam. Rogat ut in devotione Ecclesie Romane perseveret. Dat. Reate, Kalendis Aprilis, anno sexto.

Translation to English:

To the beloved son, Brother Palmerius, canon of the Holy Trinity of Campanolus, of the Order of Saint Augustine, in the diocese of Reggio. 

Our venerable brother, the Bishop of Bologna, once complained to us that the authority and commune of Bologna had usurped and disturbed the temporal jurisdiction that rightfully belongs to the Church of Bologna in the territories of San Giovanni in Persiceto, Unciola, Maximatica, Poggio d'Auliola, the Bishop's Castle, and several other castles and villages, in which it is known to have and to have been in possession of for a long time. They violently took and still hold in chains a certain man who committed murder in the said castle of San Giovanni, refusing to return him for punishment by the rector of the same castle. Therefore, through our letters, we commanded them to desist from harassing the bishop, to restore the murderer to him without any difficulty, and to allow him to exercise the aforementioned jurisdiction freely in those places. They were to appear before us by the feast of All Saints just past to do and receive what the order of justice dictated, should they claim to have any jurisdiction in the said castles and villages. However, as it is said, they contemptuously did not return the aforementioned criminal, nor did they allow the bishop to use the jurisdiction freely in those places, nor did they send a suitable representative to us. Instead, adding sin to sin, after the messengers of both parties had gone to the Apostolic See, the said authority and commune sent some of their own to investigate and punish a certain crime committed in the land of Duliola, which pertains to the jurisdiction of the same church; upon which an inquiry had been made by the bishop's messengers, and pledges and other securities had been taken from the wrongdoers. Therefore, the bishop's messengers humbly requested from us that we should take precautions to protect the rights of the Church of Bologna in these matters. Because it is very unjust and a great sacrilege to convert things given for the remedy of sins to venerable churches or left to them, or otherwise justly acquired from the faithful and Catholic men, who are obliged to preserve them, to other uses, it is right that the invaders of these things, as sacrilegious ones, should be subjected to anathema by the rectors of the churches until they make appropriate satisfaction. It is also known that, in favor of the churches, it has been introduced that the rectors of venerable places can summon their wrongdoers under whichever judge they prefer. But with the exception of jurisdiction being opposed by your messengers, it was urgently requested by them that, since an actor should regularly follow the forum of the defendant, we should leave this matter to secular judgment. Therefore, having held a careful deliberation with our brothers on these matters, we gently admonish, request, and urge them with fatherly sweetness, beseeching them for the salvation of their souls, and adjuring them by the Lord, that, humbling themselves under the mighty hand of God, since it is far more glorious to be conquered in this than to conquer, they should not refuse to receive the healing remedy, but granting these things to us freely under the hope of eternal reward, to provide due satisfaction to God and the Church concerning the aforementioned matters. To your discretion, we give an apostolic command that if it is established to you that they have invaded or disturbed the rights of the church concerning the aforementioned matters, or have invaded or disturbed them until now, you should diligently admonish them first, and compel them, by ecclesiastical censures, to desist from such actions and to make satisfaction for past damages and injuries, removing any appeal. Be careful not to pronounce sentences of excommunication or interdict against the entire community of Bologna unless you receive a special mandate from us concerning this. Given at the Lateran, on the sixth day before the kalends of February, in the sixth year of our pontificate.

REGESTO:

Gregorius IX, Brother Palmerio, canonico Sancte Trinitatis de Campanolis, ordinis Sancti Augustini, Regine diocesis, mandat ut potestas et commune Bononienses, qui jurisdictionem temporalem ecclesiae Bononiensi violentia usurpaverunt et detinuerunt homicidam a dicto episcopo puniendum, moniti desistant, et jurisdictionem restitui faciant. Dat. Laterani, VI kalendas februarii, anno sexto pontificatus nostri (1232).

To the Bishop of Le Mans, the Abbot of Pietate Dei of the Cistercian Order in the diocese of Le Mans, and the Official of Le Mans. We are compelled, not without pain of heart, to report the intolerable tyranny of the noble man G. de Lezigniaco, who, long since having put aside the fear and love of the divine name, has grievously oppressed the Malleacense monastery and its monks with the hammer of persecution. He has forced our beloved sons, the abbot and the convent, into exile, having seized the goods appointed for the use of the monks, both in head and members. He has besieged the monks in the monastery, capturing some of them and holding them in captivity until some were forced to ransom themselves. Therefore, he and his accomplices were excommunicated by apostolic authority, and his land was subjected to ecclesiastical interdict, with Christian burial prohibited there, and the body of Christ removed as it was held in contempt.

We also excommunicated him and his supporters, having our sentence published throughout the provinces of Sens, Bourges, Tours, and Bordeaux, and wherever he went, divine services were suspended as long as he remained. Later, when he promised through messengers and letters to repent and make satisfaction for the manifest damages and injuries, our venerable brothers, the Archbishop of Rouen, then Bishop of Le Mans, and the Archbishop of Tours, to whom we directed our writings on this matter, proceeded according to the form given to them to assess and estimate the manifest damages and injuries at four thousand marks of silver. We have approved their process. But he not only failed to satisfy for these but also added further grievances against the mentioned monastery. Recently, not to make satisfaction for so many and such great injuries inflicted on God and the Church, but to reduce the monastery itself to perpetual servitude, he, through his procurator and letters, made a certain grievous and burdensome composition offered before us to the abbot and the monks aforesaid.

Since he utterly despises, as if he has made a pact with death and is wholly absorbed by despair, the sentence of cursing, who should have been struck with pain and, turning back to the one striking, receive wholesome discipline, we, because it is not hoped that concerning the healing of the wound we can succeed unless we use a more severe remedy, strictly command by apostolic writings to your discretion that as long as he remains in the aforementioned sentence, you announce by our authority through the diocese of Poitiers and neighboring dioceses, that his followers are absolved from their fidelity to him, which they are not bound to keep to one who opposes God and His saints without reason. You are to compel them, as well as his confederates and others, to avoid him as excommunicated, following a prior warning, through ecclesiastical censure, with appeal removed, persuading them; indeed, if they also despise the Church's censure, fitting disgrace should not unjustly follow them as despisers of the Church's keys. And if G. does not repent even then but continues to despise ecclesiastical discipline for a longer time, he may justly dread the ingratitude of his own error, which we will make public as heretical, and the perpetual disgrace of his posterity.

Given at Rieti, on the 13th day before the Kalends of November, in the fifth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

To the archbishops of Tours and Rouen, and the bishop of Paris. It is a most unjust situation. For although the beloved sons, the Friars Minor, have wisely denied themselves and chosen to serve Christ in the highest poverty, as if possessing nothing yet having everything, there are many, both prelates of churches and others, who, led by blind greed, consider anything given to these friars by the piety of the faithful as taken away from their own avarice, and they disturb their peaceful dwellings in various ways. Even the venerable archbishops, bishops, and other prelates of churches throughout the kingdom of France, who ought to support them favorably, seek various reasons to trouble them. They wish, though not all, to hear their confessions against their will, impose penances and offer the Eucharist, and do not wish the body of Christ to be reserved in their oratories. They compel the burial of their deceased brothers in their churches and the celebration of their funerals; if any deceased brothers choose burial elsewhere than in their churches, they force the funeral to be taken first to their churches so that the offering may benefit their own uses. They do not allow them to have a bell or blessed cemetery, permitting them to celebrate divine services only at certain times. They also want to set a certain number of friars, priests, clerics, and laymen, as well as candles, lamps, and ornaments in their houses according to their will, and they demand the residue of candles when newly placed. They do not allow new priests to celebrate their first masses anywhere but in their churches, compelling them to receive and reserve offerings for their benefit in daily masses celebrated in their places and on their altars. Further, they try to extort anything given to them during the celebration of the solemnities of the Mass within the confines of their houses in the name of offerings, claiming unjustly as their right what is given to them in altar ornaments and church books, forcing them to attend their synods and be subject to their constitutions. Not content with this, they threaten to hold chapters and scrutinies in the friars’ places to correct these things, demanding fidelity sworn by oath from their ministers and guardians. They even threaten excommunication on their benefactors during winter, and the same to the friars, striving to remove them from places where they serve the Lord unless they obey in all the above matters. Furthermore, they prevent the friars, who are devoutly invited by the people, from daring to go to honorable cities and towns where they may live religiously and honestly, presuming to issue sentences of excommunication against both the entering friars and their hosts. From them, they also try to extort tithes from the fruits of gardens and rents from the friars' dwellings, as from Jewish houses, asserting that if the friars were not living there, some revenues would be paid by other inhabitants. And to bring them entirely under their dominion, they wish to appoint ministers and guardians according to their arbitrary will. Since the order of the aforesaid friars was solemnly approved by our predecessors, Innocent and Honorius, of happy memory, and by ourselves, and their rule confirmed, lest they appear to show contempt for the statutes of the Apostolic See, which they are humbly bound to accept and reverently observe, we admonish them all earnestly, giving them firm precepts through our letters to wisely consult for the safety of their conscience and reputation, and all and sundry desist entirely from the aforesaid and other grievances against them, restraining their subjects more strictly from these things. Therefore, by apostolic writings, we firmly command and mandate your fraternity that if the said archbishops, bishops, and others neglect to fulfill our precept, you compel them to observe all the aforesaid through ecclesiastical censure, removing any obstacle of contradiction and appeal. Notwithstanding any constitution, etc. But if they still care not to obey our mandates, let them know that we will otherwise provide for the aforesaid brothers, by the Lord’s authority. If not all, etc. Given at Rieti, 10th day before the Kalends of September, in the fifth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Dat. Reate, X kalendas septembris, anno quinto.

These two, sworn to faithfully execute their duty, unanimously elected seven members from the chapter, men of great honesty and religiousness, namely Master Hugo the archdeacon, and B. of Saint Mary of Montpellier, W. of Saint Mary of Melgoria, P. of Onorio, P. of Centrairanicis, A. of Saint Marcellus, and P. of Saint Eulalia, as priors of their churches, upon whom the whole chapter unanimously conferred their votes, promising that they would accept as their pastor whoever was chosen from within the body of the church. Those chosen, before all and with hands on the holy gospels, solemnly vowed that, setting aside all fear, favor, or affection, having God only before their eyes, they would elect as pastor the one whom they recognized as most useful, suitable, and competent from within the body of the church. After careful deliberation in the church in the presence of the chapter, they elected our beloved son J., the Maguelonne provost, a prudent and discreet man of noble birth and strong in influence and kinship, as bishop of Maguelonne; whom all the chapter, despite his protests and resistance, brought to the church with the singing of the "Te Deum Laudamus" and the other usual solemnities. Therefore, they asked that such a solemn, canonical, and harmonious election be confirmed by the Apostolic See; especially since our venerable brother, the Archbishop of Narbonne, the metropolitan of the place, was requested humbly to confirm it but maliciously delayed doing so; on account of which and some other grievances, an appeal was made to the Apostolic See. However, the aforementioned sacrist proposed in opposition that the said election should not be confirmed, but rather annulled and declared void, since it was of one who was bound by multiple excommunications and presumed by the excommunicated, also disregarding the aforementioned R. the archdeacon, and P. de Carnone, canon of Maguelonne, who could and should have been conveniently summoned. Hence, he requested that, the said election being annulled, we would grant him the free faculty of election. However, since the aforementioned cardinal prudently and faithfully reported these and other matters to us and our brothers, and since full faith could not be given to them before us, we have resolved, with the assent of both parties’ procurators, to commit the examination of this case to you. By apostolic writings, we command you to summon those who should be summoned for this purpose, hear the proposals from both sides, and, having rescinded whatever you find rashly attempted after the appeal to the Apostolic See from the same archbishop, if you find that the election was celebrated by the excommunicated or concerning an excommunicate, or otherwise less canonically, you should rightly annul it and provide for the said church by a canonical election of a suitable person under our authority. Otherwise, by the same authority, confirm it, and cause the due obedience and reverence to be rendered to the elect, and the consecration to be conferred. Those contradicting etc. Witnesses etc. In case not all etc., two of you etc. Given at the Lateran, on the twelfth day before the Kalends of June, in the year of our pontificate.

To the noble men, lords of Sarmiento, the spirit of wiser counsel. If, according to the wise... We have understood and indeed recount with bitterness of heart that you, because our venerable brother, the Bishop of Terracina, your diocesan, by our authority, commanded that in the same church, as in the mother church, baptism should be administered and candles blessed, where such things have traditionally been celebrated from ancient times. Therefore, lest the curse of an exasperated mother, shaking the foundations of the houses of ungrateful sons, should seem to fall upon you, whom you are bound by the precept of divine law to honor with all your might, we earnestly admonish and exhort your community, firmly commanding through apostolic letters that you cease entirely from the aforesaid grievances and molestations against the aforementioned archpriest and clerics, and henceforth permit them to celebrate the divine services and administer the aforementioned sacraments to the people of the aforesaid place in the same church, according to the mandate of the same bishop, indeed ours, without any contradiction, as has been customarily done there from ancient times. To the Archbishop of Braga. The misdeeds of P., the former bishop of Coimbra, are so numerous that they cannot be forgotten, for he has sinned against us and the Roman Church, disregarded the keys of Peter, and violated ecclesiastical authority. Not only did he recklessly violate the sentence of interdict which he had initially respected, but he also led and even forced others to ignore it. Those whom he could not sway through warnings, threats, and terrors to violate the sentence of interdict, he forced into miserable exile after atrocious injuries, the loss of goods, and the despoiling of relatives, by stripping them of dignities, prebends, and benefits. He bestowed these on his supporters, not without reckless presumption. The said bishop publicly acknowledged all these matters in our presence and that of our brothers.

Although the aforementioned bishop, not seeking judgment but mercy, voluntarily resigned into our hands, and we, compassionate towards his simplicity and old age, have not yet proceeded with the punishment his grave misconduct deserves, we do not wish for those who presumptuously violated the sentence of interdict or those who accepted the dignities, prebends, and benefits from those who were unjustly stripped of them without fault and without reasonable cause to escape canonical punishment. By the authority of Almighty God, we declare all institutions, depositions, and appointments of prebends, benefits, and dignities presumed by the same bishop, and all sentences of excommunication or interdict pronounced by him after the violation of the same interdict, to be null and void.

Given that where the offense is greater, the punishment should be more severe, so that the penalty serves as an example wherever the fault has caused scandal, we command your fraternity by apostolic writings to entirely remove all those whom the said bishop intruded into the aforementioned benefits, prebends, and dignities, not only from those posts but also from any other benefits or churches they might hold, notwithstanding an appeal they claim to have made from your vicar. We also instruct you to fully restore all those dispossessed on this occasion without any difficulty. Suspend both the usurpers and others who reprehensibly violated the interdict from office and benefit, and declare excommunicated those who laid violent hands on the clergy, compelling them to come to us within four months to receive their due judgment, using, if necessary, the help of secular authorities.

Lest P., the treasurer, P. Gonsalvi, and Johannes Fernandi, canons of Coimbra, and others who have been dispossessed be forced to beg, bringing disgrace upon the clerical order, especially since they should have earned a reward for such an honest and commendable cause, we wish and command that they be suitably provided for from the goods of the Church of Coimbra until they regain peaceful possession of their dignities and benefits. Furthermore, because an evil minister sometimes has workers of iniquity, do not neglect to require Master Gonsalvus and Alfonsus Menendi, relatives of the same bishop, whom he left as his vicars, to account for the fruits of the bishopric of Coimbra, and also Alfonsus Menendi for the treasury and instruments of the church. Opponents, etc. No letters to the contrary, etc. Given at Spoleto, the 7th calends of July, in the year.

To the Bishop of Astorga, the Bishop of Lugo, and the Dean of Lugo. From the special affection of love we bear towards our dearest son in Christ, the illustrious King of Portugal, who is still in his minority, we zealously seek his well-being with paternal diligence. We desire that, exercising the first fruits of his youth in the fear of the divine name and in love, he may raise his sight to Him who alone rules in the kingdom of men, who deposes the mighty from their thrones and exalts the humble, so that after the necessary end of this present life, he may happily pass from a temporal kingdom to an eternal one. Whether they find women with them or not, they defame them and seize their goods; because of this, several clerics, forced to buy off such harassment, especially to avoid damage to their reputation, pay certain tributes annually to these officials, to the severe injury and loss of the ecclesiastical order. If the bishop and his archdeacons proceed against any cleric, punishing him as his offense demands, the aforementioned king, when the cleric appeals to him, compels the bishop and archdeacons to restore him by seizing ecclesiastical goods, or has him restored fully by his porter, due to which many offenses remain uncorrected. Furthermore, the king frequently occupies the bishopric and the goods of the Greater Church and the churches of his diocese by his authority, taking any opportunity against them. If a cleric is summoned by a layman in secular judgment over ecclesiastical possession and refuses to contest jurisdiction in that forum, the claimant is immediately placed in possession of the disputed property, forcing the cleric, willingly or unwillingly, to lose possession or to litigate before a judge not of his own. Moreover, what is more serious, clerics are compelled to undergo secular judgment in both criminal and civil matters, against legitimate and canonical sanctions. If some are cut off by the sentence of excommunication from the unity of the church, they are not avoided by him as is expedient and fitting to the king's honor, as they might sooner be reconciled and return more swiftly to salvation. Moreover, Jews in the bishopric of Lisbon are openly preferred in public offices, contrary to the statutes of the general council, to the disgrace of the Christian faith and the grave scandal of many. Furthermore, the king imposes collections, exactions, and various services and demands through himself or his agents upon churches and ecclesiastical persons, extorting pledges from them at will, and leads clerics into military service, and for guard duties and watch duties, to use the words of that land, and compels them, against ecclesiastical liberty, to build towers and guard them except for the towers of their own places where they reside, and to keep falconers and dogs in their homes and supply their needs. To the Chapter of Bayeux. It is read in Genesis that Tamar, having received the ring, bracelet, and staff, conceived by Judah, and when the time of delivery was approaching, two twins appeared in her womb. One put out his hand, on which the midwife is said to have tied a scarlet thread; and when he drew back his hand, the other, namely Perez, came forth. For Tamar is interpreted as "palm tree," which is a beautiful and fruitful tree, signifying the church of Bayeux, which is accustomed to be beautiful in the decorum of knowledge and fruitful in the abundance of good works. This church, having received faith in the ring, work in the bracelet, and the support of the poor and weak in the staff, conceived from the seed of the true Judah when it proposed to create a pastor by divine inspiration. To A. of Samathia, Petragoricensis, and Master Durandus, Archdeacons of Limoges, and the Prior of St. Radegund of Poitiers. The humble teaching of the master instructed the humble disciples to have salt in themselves and peace among themselves in such a way that the gentleness of peace may soothe the salt of wisdom, and the salt of wisdom may season the gentleness of peace. There are indeed some who, by stirring up strife under the guise of zeal for souls, taste only that which is salty, and fall into injury under the guise of justice, splitting hearts with discord, as they dig wells of quarreling and enmity, without considering that, Isaac, having left the wells of contention in contempt, dug another for which the shepherds did not contend, whose name was called 'broadness,' because charity is constrained when contention spreads, and if contention is narrowed, charity is expanded. Hence, concord must be restored to hearts so that the work of justice is peace and its cultivation is silence, especially in those who, with the silvered wings of the dove, ought to shine as peacemakers both for themselves and for their subjects, sitting in the beauty of peace, in tabernacles of confidence and abundant rest. Indeed, it has not escaped the notice of neighbors and has reached many far-off places how much grievance the question of primacy raised between the churches of Bourges and Bordeaux and their prelates has caused and would cause in the future if it were to endure, considering past conjectures. Lawsuits are accustomed to be prodigal of expenses, generous of labors, sparing of modesty, greedy of rest, and would that they were not incentives of agitation and discord, because rarely does the tongue remain silent in the quarrel of disputes, and rarely does the mind rest amid the noise of judgments. However, the venerable brothers, the archbishops of Bourges and Bordeaux, considering the dangers to souls that threaten their churches from their absence and that the life of the cause seemed to bring about a certain death, humbly requested that the question whose judgment was prolonged by duration be shortened by the acceleration of providence. They entrusted all rights pertaining to themselves and their churches to the provision of the Apostolic See. We, considering that among the three things that are read as proven before God and men, brotherly concord holds the first place, have admitted the submitted petition to the grace of hearing, favorably pursuing their desires. However, lest we seem to omit anything of what pertains, we command with the consent of both parties, that you seek the consent of the prelates of the province of Bordeaux present there, and of the cathedral chapters of the same province, as well as the chapter of Bourges on the aforesaid matters. Once obtained, you shall solemnly publish the provision fortified by our bull, which we send to you enclosed in another letter. However, if there are any who, which we do not believe, are unwilling to give consent, you shall abstain from the aforesaid publication and strictly command them under a specified time limit which you deem appropriate that they personally, if they are prelates, or if others, through suitable procurators, present themselves before us, to prosecute before us any right they claim to have, answer the other party concerning those things they propose, and, if they should perhaps succumb, satisfy expenses. If not all, etc. Given at Rieti, 4th of the Kalends of April, in the sixth year.
